title.raw: 卷十六 列傳第六 王鎮惡 朱齡石 毛脩之 傅弘之 朱脩之 王玄謨 Volume 16 Biographies 6: Wwang Zhene, Zhu Lingshi, Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi, Zhu Xiuzhi, Wang Xuanmo

sentences.zh: 列傳第六

translations.literal: Biographies 6
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 6

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡朱齡石毛修之傅弘之朱修之王玄謨

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e, Zhu Lingshi, Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi, Zhu Xiuzhi, Wang Xuanmo
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e, Zhu Lingshi, Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi, Zhu Xiuzhi, and Wang Xuanmo

sentences.zh: 王镇恶，北海剧人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e was a man of Ju in Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e came from Ju in Beihai commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖猛，仕苻坚，任兼将相。

translations.literal: His grandfather Meng served Fu Jian, holding posts of general and minister together.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Meng had served Fu Jian of Former Qin, rising to joint command of armies and state.

sentences.zh: 父休，为河东太守。

translations.literal: His father Xiu was Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiu served as Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 镇恶以五月生，家人以俗忌，欲令出继疏宗。

translations.literal: Zhen'e was born in the fifth month; the family, because of popular taboo, wished to have him adopted out to a distant branch.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the fifth month—a month of ill omen—his family wanted to give him away to a collateral line.

sentences.zh: 猛曰："此非常儿。

translations.literal: Meng said, "This is no ordinary child.
translations.idiomatic: Meng said, "This is no ordinary boy.

sentences.zh: 昔孟尝君恶月生而相齐，是儿亦将兴吾门矣。

translations.literal: In old times Lord Mengchang, though born in an ill month, became prime minister of Qi; this boy too will raise our house."
translations.idiomatic: Lord Mengchang of old was born under an unlucky sign yet rose to rule Qi; this child will do the same for us."

sentences.zh: "故名为镇恶。

translations.literal: Therefore he was named Zhen'e—"subdues evil."
translations.idiomatic: So they named him Zhen'e—"subduer of evil."

sentences.zh: 年十三而苻氏败，寓食渑池人李方家。

translations.literal: At thirteen the Fu clan fell; he lodged and ate at the home of Li Fang of Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen, when the Fu regime collapsed, he found shelter with Li Fang of Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 方善遇之，谓方曰："若遭英雄主，要取万户侯，当厚相报。

translations.literal: Fang treated him well; Zhen'e told Fang, "If I meet a heroic lord and win a marquisate of ten thousand households, I shall repay you generously."
translations.idiomatic: Fang treated him kindly. Zhen'e said to him, "Should I find a great patron and win a ten-thousand-household fief, I will reward you handsomely."

sentences.zh: "方曰："君丞相孙，人材如此，何患不富贵，至时愿见用为本县令足矣。

translations.literal: Fang said, "You are the grandson of a chief minister, and talent such as yours—what need to fear lack of wealth? When that day comes, I would be content to see you appoint me magistrate of this county."
translations.idiomatic: Fang replied, "You are a prime minister's grandson, with gifts like these—why worry about rank? When the time comes, let me be magistrate here and I will be satisfied."

sentences.zh: " 後隨叔父曜歸晉，客荊州，頗讀諸子兵書，喜論軍國大事，騎射非長，而從橫善果斷。

translations.literal: Later he followed his uncle Yao back to Jin, sojourned in Jing Province, read widely in the military classics, delighted in discussing grand affairs of army and state; he was no master of horsemanship and archery, yet in boldness and decisiveness he excelled.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed his uncle Yao into Jin service and lived in Jing Province. He studied the military classics and loved to debate strategy and statecraft. Riding and shooting were not his strengths, but he was bold and resolute.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝伐廣固，鎮惡時為天門郡臨澧令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song attacked Guanggu, Zhen'e was magistrate of Linli in Tianmen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song campaign against Guanggu, Zhen'e held the post of magistrate of Linli in Tianmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 人或薦之武帝，召與語，異焉，因留宿。

translations.literal: Someone recommended him to the Emperor; the Emperor summoned and spoke with him, found him remarkable, and kept him overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Someone brought him to the Emperor's attention. Summoned for an audience, he so impressed the ruler that he was asked to stay the night.

sentences.zh: 旦謂諸佐曰：「鎮惡王猛孫，所謂將門有將。

translations.literal: In the morning the Emperor told his aides, "Zhen'e is Wang Meng's grandson—the saying goes, general's households breed generals.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Emperor told his staff, "Zhen'e is Wang Meng's grandson. As they say, a general's house breeds generals.

sentences.zh: 」即以署前部賊曹。

translations.literal: " He at once appointed him to the post of chief of the vanguard bandit-suppression bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately made him chief of the vanguard bandit-suppression bureau.

sentences.zh: 拒盧循有功，封博陸縣五等子。

translations.literal: For repelling Lu Xun he earned merit and was enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Viscount of Bolu.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Lu Xun he was rewarded with a fifth-rank viscounty at Bolu.

sentences.zh: 武帝謀討劉毅，鎮惡曰：「公若有事西楚，請給百舸為前驅。

translations.literal: When the Emperor planned to attack Liu Yi, Zhen'e said, "If my lord undertakes business in the western Chu region, grant me a hundred warships as vanguard."
translations.idiomatic: Planning the campaign against Liu Yi, Zhen'e offered, "If you move against the west, give me a hundred ships to lead the way."

sentences.zh: 」及西討，轉鎮惡參軍事，使率龍驤將軍蒯恩百舸前發。

translations.literal: When the western campaign began, he was transferred to Zhen'e's staff as adjutant and ordered to lead General of Dragon Valor Kuai En's hundred warships forward.
translations.idiomatic: On the western expedition he became a staff adjutant and was sent ahead with Kuai En's hundred dragon-valor warships.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡受命，便晝夜兼行，揚聲劉兗州上。

translations.literal: Zhen'e received the order and at once marched day and night, spreading word that he was bound for Governor Liu's province.
translations.idiomatic: Taking command, he forced the march day and night while letting it be known he was sailing for Liu Yi's province.

sentences.zh: 毅謂為信，不知見襲。

translations.literal: Yi believed it and did not know he was being struck.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took the report at face value and never suspected an attack.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡去江陵城二十里，舍船步上，蒯恩軍在前，鎮惡次之，舸留一二人，對舸岸上豎旗安鼓。

translations.literal: Twenty li from Jiangling city, Zhen'e abandoned ship and went on foot; Kuai En's troops led, Zhen'e followed, and on each boat one or two men were left to set flags and drums on the bank opposite.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li from Jiangling he beached the fleet and marched ashore—Kuai En in front, Zhen'e behind—leaving one or two men per boat to raise flags and beat drums on the opposite bank.

sentences.zh: 語所留人曰：「計我將至城，便長嚴，令如後有大軍狀。

translations.literal: He told those left behind, "When I am about to reach the city, sound the long roll at once and make it seem a great army follows."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed the rear guard, "When I near the walls, beat the long roll and make it look as though a host is coming behind me."

sentences.zh: 又分隊在後，令燒江津船。

translations.literal: He also split detachments to the rear with orders to burn the boats at the Jiang crossing.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent parties to the rear with orders to burn the boats at the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡徑前襲城，津戍及百姓皆言劉藩實上，晏然不疑。

translations.literal: Zhen'e went straight to storm the city; the ferry guards and townspeople all said Liu Fan was truly arriving, and remained calm and unsuspecting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e struck directly for the city. Ferry guards and townsfolk alike assumed Liu Fan was truly coming and never grew alarmed.

sentences.zh: 將至城，逢毅要將朱顯之馳前問藩所在，軍人答云：「在後」。

translations.literal: As he neared the city he met Yi's chief officer Zhu Xianzhi, who galloped forward asking where Fan was; the soldiers answered, "In the rear."
translations.idiomatic: Near the walls he met Yi's officer Zhu Xianzhi, who rode up demanding Liu Fan's whereabouts; the men answered, "In the rear."

sentences.zh: 及至軍後不見藩，又望見江津船艦被燒而鼓聲甚盛，知非藩上，便躍馬告毅，令閉城門。

translations.literal: When he reached the rear of the army and saw no Fan, and looked again to see boats at the Jiang crossing burning while drums thundered, he knew it was not Fan and at once leapt on horseback to tell Yi to shut the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the rear and finding no Fan, he saw the crossing ablaze and drums roaring—clearly not Liu Fan. He spurred his horse to warn Yi to shut the gates.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡亦馳進得入城，便因風放火，燒大城南門及東門。

translations.literal: Zhen'e also galloped in and entered the city, then set fire with the wind, burning the great city's south and east gates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e galloped in after him, then turned the wind to flame and burned the south and east gates of the inner city.

sentences.zh: 又遣人以詔及赦文並武帝手書凡三函示毅，毅皆燒不視。

translations.literal: He also sent men to show Yi three packets—the imperial edict, the amnesty, and the Emperor's own letter; Yi burned them all unread.
translations.idiomatic: He also had three packets delivered—an edict, an amnesty, and the Emperor's own letter. Yi burned every one without reading them.

sentences.zh: 金城內亦未信帝自來。

translations.literal: Within the Golden City too they still did not believe the Emperor had come in person.
translations.idiomatic: Even inside the Golden City they still refused to believe the Emperor had come himself.

sentences.zh: 及短兵接戰，鎮惡軍人與毅下將或是父兄子弟中表親親，且鬥且語，知武帝在後，人情離懈。

translations.literal: When close combat began, Zhen'e's soldiers and Yi's subordinates were often fathers and sons, brothers, cousins, and kin by marriage; as they fought they spoke, learned the Emperor was behind them, and hearts slackened.
translations.idiomatic: In the close fighting, many of Zhen'e's men faced Yi's troops who were fathers, sons, brothers, or cousins. As they traded blows they talked—and once they knew the Emperor was behind Zhen'e, Yi's ranks lost heart.

sentences.zh: 初，毅常所乘馬在城外不得入，倉卒無馬，使就子肅取馬，肅不與。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yi's usual mount was outside the city and could not enter; in haste with no horse, he sent to his son Su for one, and Su refused.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's own horse was trapped outside the walls. With no mount at hand he sent to his son Su for a horse; Su would not give one.

sentences.zh: 朱顯之謂曰：「人取汝父而惜馬，汝走欲何之？

translations.literal: Zhu Xianzhi said to Su, "Men are taking your father and you begrudge a horse—where do you think you can run?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xianzhi snapped at Su, "They are seizing your father and you hoard a horse—where do you expect to flee?"

sentences.zh: 」奪馬以授毅，從大城東門出奔牛牧佛寺自縊。

translations.literal: He seized the horse and gave it to Yi, who fled out the great city's east gate to Niufu Buddhist temple and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrested the horse away and gave it to Yi, who rode out the east gate to Niufu Temple and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡身被五箭，手所執矟於手中破折。

translations.literal: Zhen'e himself took five arrows; the spear he held snapped in his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e took five arrow wounds himself, and the spear in his grip shattered mid-fight.

sentences.zh: 江陵平後二十日，大軍方至，以功封漢壽縣子。

translations.literal: Twenty days after Jiangling was pacified the main army arrived; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Hanshou.
translations.idiomatic: The main army arrived twenty days after Jiangling fell. For this victory he received the viscounty of Hanshou.

sentences.zh: 及武帝北伐，為鎮西諮議，行龍驤將軍，領前鋒。

translations.literal: When the Emperor marched north, Zhen'e was advisory officer of the Pacifying West command, acting General of Dragon Valor, leading the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern expedition he served as Pacifying West adviser, acting Dragon Valor general, and vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 將發，前將軍劉穆之謂曰：「昔晉文王委蜀于鄧艾，今亦委卿以關中，卿其勉之。

translations.literal: Before departure the Forward General Liu Muzhi told him, "In old days Jin's Prince Wen entrusted Shu to Deng Ai; today I entrust Guanzhong to you— exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Before the march Liu Muzhi told him, "Prince Wen of Jin once entrusted Shu to Deng Ai; today I entrust Guanzhong to you. Do not fail me."

sentences.zh: 」鎮惡曰：「吾等因托風雲，並蒙抽擢，今咸陽不克，誓不濟江。

translations.literal: Zhen'e said, "We have all ridden fortune's wind and been plucked up together; if Xianyang is not taken, I swear not to cross the river again."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e replied, "We have all risen on the same tide. If we do not take Xianyang, I will not recross the river alive."

sentences.zh: 三秦若定，而公九錫不至，亦卿之責矣。」

translations.literal: If the Three Qins are settled and yet your nine bestowals do not arrive, that too will be your fault."
translations.idiomatic: And if the Three Qin are pacified yet the nine bestowals never come—that will be your burden as well."

sentences.zh: 鎮惡入賊境，戰無不捷，破虎牢及柏穀塢。

translations.literal: Entering enemy territory, Zhen'e was victorious in every battle, taking Hulao and Baigu Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside enemy lands he did not lose a battle, capturing Hulao and Baigu Stockade.

sentences.zh: 進次澠池，造故人李方家，升堂見母，厚加酬賚，即授方澠池令。

translations.literal: Advancing to Mianchi he came to his old friend Li Fang's house, entered the hall and saw Fang's mother, rewarded them generously, and at once made Fang magistrate of Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: At Mianchi he visited his old host Li Fang, bowed to Fang's mother, lavished gifts upon them, and appointed Fang magistrate on the spot.

sentences.zh: 方軌徑據潼關，將士乏食，乃親到弘農督人租。

translations.literal: Fang's troops pressed on and seized Tong Pass; the officers and soldiers lacked food, so he personally went to Hongnong to press grain levies.
translations.idiomatic: His column seized Tong Pass, but supplies ran short; he went in person to Hongnong to drive the grain levy.

sentences.zh: 百姓競送義粟，軍食復振。

translations.literal: The people competed to send voluntary grain; army provisions revived.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners vied to bring voluntary grain, and the army's stores filled again.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝與鎮惡等期，若克洛陽，須待大軍，未可輕前。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor had agreed with Zhen'e and the others that if Luoyang fell they must wait for the main army and not advance lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had agreed beforehand that if Luoyang fell they must wait for the main army and not press forward rashly.

sentences.zh: 既而鎮惡等至潼關，為偽大將軍姚紹所拒不得進，馳告武帝求糧援。

translations.literal: Presently Zhen'e and the others reached Tong Pass and were blocked by the false Grand General Yao Shao and could not advance; they galloped to tell the Emperor and beg grain and reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass they were stopped by Yao Shao and could not break through. Zhen'e sent riders to the Emperor begging food and reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 時帝軍入河，魏軍屯河岸，軍不得進。

translations.literal: Then the Emperor's army entered the Yellow River; Wei troops camped on the north bank and the army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Emperor had entered the Yellow River, but Wei forces held the north bank and blocked all movement.

sentences.zh: 帝呼所遣人開舫北戶指河上軍示之曰：「我語令勿進而深入，岸上如此，何由得遣軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor called the messenger, opened the north hatch of the boat, pointed at the army on the river and showed him, saying, "I told you not to advance yet you went deep; with the north bank like this, how can I send troops?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor opened the north hatch of his boat, pointed at the army on the riverbank, and said, "I ordered you not to go deep—look at the north shore. How am I to send help?"

sentences.zh: 」鎮惡既得義租，紹又病死，偽撫軍將軍姚贊代紹守嶮，眾力猶盛。

translations.literal: Once Zhen'e had the voluntary grain, Shao also died of illness; the false Pacifying Army General Yao Zan replaced Shao in guarding the passes, and their strength was still great.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e secured the voluntary grain just as Shao died. Yao Zan replaced him on the passes, and enemy strength remained formidable.

sentences.zh: 武帝至湖城，贊引退。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Hucheng, Zan withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor reached Hucheng, Zan pulled back.

sentences.zh: 大軍次潼關，謀進取計，鎮惡請率水軍自河入渭，直至渭橋。

translations.literal: The main army halted at Tong Pass to plan the advance; Zhen'e asked to lead the navy from the river into the Wei and straight to Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass the high command debated next steps. Zhen'e proposed leading the fleet up the Wei River straight to Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡所乘皆蒙沖小艦，行船者悉在艦內，泝渭而進，艦外不見有行船人。

translations.literal: The boats Zhen'e rode were all covered assault craft; those who rowed were all inside the hull; they went upstream on the Wei, and from outside the boats no rowers could be seen.
translations.idiomatic: His fleet was all covered assault boats with rowers hidden inside the hull. They ascended the Wei, and from the bank no oarsmen could be seen.

sentences.zh: 北土素無舟烜，莫不驚以為神。

translations.literal: The north had never known boats and fires; all were startled and took it for divine.
translations.idiomatic: Boats were unknown in the north; everyone was stunned and called it sorcery.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡既至，令將士食畢，便棄船登岸。

translations.literal: When Zhen'e arrived he ordered officers and soldiers to eat their fill, then abandoned the boats and went ashore.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he let the men eat their fill, then ordered them to abandon the boats and land.

sentences.zh: 渭水流急，諸艦悉逐流去，鎮惡撫慰士卒曰：「此是長安城北門外，去家萬里，而舫乘衣糧並已逐流，唯宜死戰，可立大功。

translations.literal: The Wei River ran swift; all the boats were swept downstream. Zhen'e comforted the troops, saying, "This is outside the north gate of Chang'an, ten thousand li from home; boats, clothes, and grain have all been swept away—only death in battle can win great merit."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ran fast and every boat was swept away. He rallied the men: "We stand outside Chang'an's north gate, ten thousand li from home. Boats, clothes, grain—all gone. Only a fight to the death will win glory."

sentences.zh: 」乃身先士卒，即陷長安城。

translations.literal: Then he led from the front and at once stormed Chang'an city.
translations.idiomatic: He charged at the head of the column and took Chang'an in one assault.

sentences.zh: 城內六萬餘戶，鎮惡撫慰初附，號令嚴肅。

translations.literal: Within the city were more than sixty thousand households; Zhen'e soothed the newly submitted, and his orders were stern.
translations.idiomatic: The city held more than sixty thousand households. Zhen'e pacified the newly surrendered with strict but fair discipline.

sentences.zh: 于灞上奉迎，武帝勞之曰：「成吾霸業者真卿也。

translations.literal: At Bashang he went to meet the Emperor; the Emperor praised him, saying, "You, sir, have fulfilled my hegemony."
translations.idiomatic: At Bashang he welcomed the Emperor, who told him, "You have made my empire real."

sentences.zh: 」謝曰：「此明公之威，諸將之力。

translations.literal: He thanked him, saying, "This is my lord's majesty and the generals' strength."
translations.idiomatic: He demurred: "This is your majesty's authority and the generals' labor."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「卿欲學馮異邪。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Do you wish to imitate Feng Yi?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed. "Trying to play Feng Yi, are you?"

sentences.zh: 時關中豐全，鎮惡性貪，收斂子女玉帛不可勝計，帝以其功大不問。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong was rich and full; Zhen'e was greedy by nature and gathered women, jade, and silk beyond counting; the Emperor, because his merit was great, did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was flush with wealth, and Zhen'e's greed knew no bounds—women, jade, silk piled beyond reckoning. The Emperor let it pass because of his service.

sentences.zh: 時有白帝言鎮惡藏姚泓偽輦，有異志，帝使覘之，知鎮惡剔取飾輦金銀，棄輦於垣側，帝乃安。

translations.literal: At the time someone reported to the Emperor that Zhen'e had hidden Yao Hong's false imperial carriage and had different intent; the Emperor sent men to spy and learned Zhen'e had stripped the carriage's gold and silver ornaments and cast the carriage by a wall; the Emperor then was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused him of hoarding Yao Hong's imperial carriage as proof of rebellion. Spies found he had stripped its gold and silver and dumped the frame by a wall. The Emperor's suspicions eased.

sentences.zh: 帝留第二子桂陽公義真為安西將軍、雍秦二州刺史，鎮長安。

translations.literal: The Emperor left his second son, the Duke of Guiyang Yizhen, as General Pacifying the West and Governor of Yong and Qin, stationed at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor left his second son, Duke of Guiyang Yizhen, as Pacifying West general and governor of Yong and Qin, garrisoned at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡以征虜將軍領安西司馬、馮翊太守，委以扞禦之任。

translations.literal: Zhen'e, as General Subduing Barbarians, held the post of Pacifying West staff major and Administrator of Fengyi, entrusted with the duty of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e served as Subduing Barbarians general, Pacifying West staff major, and Fengyi administrator, charged with the frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 及大軍東還，赫連勃勃逼北地，義真遣中兵參軍沈田子拒之。

translations.literal: When the main army returned east, Helian Bobo pressed Beidi; Yizhen sent staff officer Shen Tianzi to resist.
translations.idiomatic: As the main army marched east, Helian Bobo pressed Beidi. Yizhen sent staff officer Shen Tianzi to hold him off.

sentences.zh: 虜甚盛，田子退屯劉因堡，遣使還報鎮惡。

translations.literal: The barbarians were very strong; Tianzi withdrew to camp at Liuyin Fort and sent a messenger back to report to Zhen'e.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy force was overwhelming. Tianzi fell back to Liuyin Fort and sent a messenger to Zhen'e.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡對田子使謂安西長史王修曰：「公以十歲兒付吾等，當共思竭力，今擁兵不進，賊何由得平？

translations.literal: Zhen'e replied to Tianzi's messenger through Pacifying West chief clerk Wang Xiu, saying, "The Duke entrusted a ten-year-old boy to us—we should all think and exert ourselves with full strength; now you hold troops and do not advance—how can the bandits be crushed?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e answered through chief clerk Wang Xiu: "They left a ten-year-old in our care. We must all give everything. You sit on your troops and refuse to advance—how will the enemy ever be beaten?"

sentences.zh: 」使反言之，田子甚懼。

translations.literal: He had the reply sent back; Tianzi was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the message back through Tianzi's courier. Tianzi was terrified.

sentences.zh: 王猛之相苻堅也，北人以方諸葛亮。

translations.literal: When Wang Meng served as Fu Jian's minister, northerners compared him to Zhuge Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Meng served Fu Jian, northerners had likened him to Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 入關之功，又鎮惡為首，時論者深憚之。

translations.literal: The merit of entering the passes was led by Zhen'e; men of the time deeply feared this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e had led the conquest of the passes, and contemporaries feared his stature.

sentences.zh: 田子嶢柳之捷，威震三輔，而與鎮惡爭功。

translations.literal: Tianzi's victory at Yaoliu shook the Three Auxiliaries, yet he contended with Zhen'e for credit.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi's victory at Yaoliu had made him a hero of the Three Auxiliaries, yet he quarreled with Zhen'e over credit.

sentences.zh: 武帝將歸，留田子與鎮惡，私謂田子曰：「鍾會不得遂其亂者，為有衛瓘等也。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to return, he left Tianzi with Zhen'e and privately told Tianzi, "Zhong Hui could not finish his rebellion because men like Wei Guan stood against him.
translations.idiomatic: Before returning east the Emperor left Tianzi with Zhen'e and told him privately, "Zhong Hui's plot failed because Wei Guan and others checked him.

sentences.zh: 語曰：'猛獸不如群狐。

translations.literal: The saying goes: 'A lone beast is no match for a pack of foxes.'
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, 'One tiger is no match for a den of foxes.'"

sentences.zh: '卿等十餘人何懼王鎮惡。

translations.literal: Why should you dozen-odd men fear Wang Zhen'e?"
translations.idiomatic: What need have you dozen men to fear Wang Zhen'e?"

sentences.zh: 」故二人常有猜心。

translations.literal: Therefore the two men always harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the two men watched each other with suspicion.

sentences.zh: 時鎮惡師於涇上，與田子俱會傅弘之壘，田子求屏人，因斬之幕下，並兄基弟鴻、遵、深從弟昭、朗、弘，凡七人。

translations.literal: At that time Zhen'e encamped on the Jing River and met Tianzi at Fu Hongzhi's fort; Tianzi asked to speak in private and cut him down beneath the tent, together with his elder brother Ji, younger brothers Hong, Zun, and Shen, cousins Zhao and Lang, and Hong—seven men in all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen'e was camped on the Jing when he met Tianzi at Fu Hongzhi's fort. Tianzi asked for a private word and cut him down in the tent—along with his brothers Ji, Hong, Zun, and Shen, his cousins Zhao and Lang, and Hong. Seven men in all.

sentences.zh: 弘之奔告義真，義真率王智、王修被甲登橫門以察其變。

translations.literal: Hongzhi ran to tell Yizhen; Yizhen led Wang Zhi and Wang Xiu in armor up Heng Gate to observe the disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi fled to warn Yizhen, who armored Wang Zhi and Wang Xiu and climbed Heng Gate to see what had happened.

sentences.zh: 俄而田子至，言鎮惡反。

translations.literal: Presently Tianzi arrived and said Zhen'e had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzi arrived moments later and claimed Zhen'e had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 修執田子，以專戮斬焉。

translations.literal: Xiu seized Tianzi and executed him for unauthorized killing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiu seized Tianzi and executed him for killing without authority.

sentences.zh: 是歲，義熙十四年正月十五日也。

translations.literal: It was the fifteenth day of the first month in the fourteenth year of Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fifteenth day of the first month, Yixi year 14.

sentences.zh: 追贈左將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Left General and Governor of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Left General and Governor of Qing.

sentences.zh: 及帝受命，追封龍陽縣侯，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the Mandate, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Longyang, posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was founded he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Longyang with the posthumous name Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 傳國至曾孫叡，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: The fief passed to his great-grandson Rui; when Qi received the abdication the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to his great-grandson Rui until Qi took the throne and abolished the fief.

sentences.zh: 朱齡石字伯兒，沛郡沛人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Lingshi, styled Bo'er, was a man of Pei in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi, styled Bo'er, came from Pei in Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 世為將，伯父憲及斌並為西中郎袁真將佐。

translations.literal: For generations his family were generals; his father's elder brothers Xian and Bin were both staff officers to Western Central Commander Yuan Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: His family had produced generals for generations. His uncles Xian and Bin both served Yuan Zhen, Western Central Commander.

sentences.zh: 桓溫伐真于壽陽，真以憲兄弟潛通溫，並殺之，齡石父綽逃歸溫。

translations.literal: When Huan Wen attacked Zhen at Shouyang, Zhen because the Xian brothers secretly communicated with Wen killed them both; Lingshi's father Chuo fled back to Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen besieged Zhen at Shouyang, Zhen discovered the Xian brothers were in secret contact with Wen and had them killed. Lingshi's father Chuo fled to Wen.

sentences.zh: 壽陽平，真已死，綽輒發棺戮屍。

translations.literal: When Shouyang was pacified and Zhen was already dead, Chuo at once opened the coffin and dismembered the corpse.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouyang fell and Zhen was dead, Chuo opened the coffin and mutilated the corpse.

sentences.zh: 溫怒將斬之，溫弟沖請得免。

translations.literal: Wen in anger was about to execute him; Wen's younger brother Chong pleaded and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was furious and meant to kill him, but Wen's brother Chong interceded and saved his life.

sentences.zh: 綽受沖更生之恩，事沖如父。

translations.literal: Chuo received Chong's grace of renewed life and served Chong as a father.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo owed Chong his life and served him as he would a father.

sentences.zh: 位西陽、廣平太守。

translations.literal: He reached the posts of Administrator of Xiyang and Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administer Xiyang and Guangping.

sentences.zh: 及沖薨，綽歐血而死。

translations.literal: When Chong died, Chuo vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong died, Chuo vomited blood and followed him.

sentences.zh: 齡石少好武，不事崖檢。

translations.literal: Lingshi in youth loved martial arts and did not attend to propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Young Lingshi loved fighting and cared little for decorum.

sentences.zh: 舅淮南蔣氏才劣，齡石使舅臥聽事，翦紙方寸帖著舅枕，以刀子縣擲之，相去八九尺，百擲百中。

translations.literal: His maternal uncle of the Jiang family in Huainan was untalented; Lingshi had the uncle lie in the reception hall, pasted a square inch of paper on the uncle's pillow, and with a knife suspended and thrown from eight or nine chi away, hit it every time out of a hundred throws.
translations.idiomatic: His Huainan uncle Jiang was a mediocrity. Lingshi made him lie in the hall, stuck a square of paper on his pillow, and from eight or nine feet away threw a knife suspended on a string—a hundred throws, a hundred hits.

sentences.zh: 舅畏齡石，終不敢動。

translations.literal: The uncle feared Lingshi and never dared move.
translations.idiomatic: The uncle was so terrified he never dared stir.

sentences.zh: 舅頭有大瘤，齡石伺眠密割之即死。

translations.literal: The uncle had a large wen on his head; Lingshi waited until he slept and secretly cut it off, and he died at once.
translations.idiomatic: The uncle had a large wen on his head. Lingshi waited until he slept, cut it off in secret, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 武帝克京城，以為建武參軍。

translations.literal: When the Emperor took the capital, Lingshi was made adjutant of the Jianwu command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor captured the capital, Lingshi was appointed adjutant on the Jianwu staff.

sentences.zh: 從至江乘將戰，齡石言世受桓氏恩，不容以兵刃相向，乞在軍後。

translations.literal: Following to Jiangcheng when battle was imminent, Lingshi said his family had long received the Huan clan's grace and could not bear to meet them with arms, and begged to remain in the rear of the army.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangcheng, on the eve of battle, he said his family owed the Huans a debt of gratitude and he could not cross blades with them. He asked to stay in the rear.

sentences.zh: 帝義而許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor in righteousness permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, moved by his loyalty, agreed.

sentences.zh: 以為鎮軍參軍，遷武康令。

translations.literal: He was made adjutant of the Pacifying Army and transferred to magistrate of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Pacifying Army adjutant, then magistrate of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 縣人姚系祖專為劫，郡縣畏不能討，齡石至縣，偽與厚，召為參軍。

translations.literal: A man of the county, Yao Jizu, specialized in robbery; the commandery and county feared him and could not suppress him; when Lingshi arrived he feigned friendship, summoned him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: A local bandit, Yao Jizu, had terrorized the district until no magistrate dared move against him. Lingshi feigned friendship and summoned him as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 系祖恃強，乃出應召。

translations.literal: Jizu relied on his strength and therefore came out to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his power, Jizu walked into the trap.

sentences.zh: 齡石斬之，掩其家，悉殺其兄弟，由是一部得清。

translations.literal: Lingshi beheaded him, raided his house, and killed all his brothers; from this the whole region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi cut off his head, stormed his house, and killed every brother in the clan. The whole region was pacified at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 後領中兵。

translations.literal: Later he led the central army.
translations.idiomatic: He later commanded the central corps.

sentences.zh: 齡石有武幹，又練吏職，帝甚親委之。

translations.literal: Lingshi had martial talent and was also skilled in administrative duties; the Emperor greatly trusted and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi combined battlefield skill with administrative competence, and the Emperor relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 平盧循有功，為西陽太守。

translations.literal: For pacifying Lu Xun he earned merit and was made Administrator of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Lu Xun he was made Administrator of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 義熙九年，徙益州刺史，為元帥伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi he was transferred to Governor of Yizhou as supreme commander to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 9 he was transferred to Governor of Yizhou and given supreme command of the Shu expedition.

sentences.zh: 初，帝與齡石密謀進取，曰：「劉敬宣往年出黃武，無功而退。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor and Lingshi secretly planned the advance, saying, "Liu Jingxuan in former years went out by Huangwu and withdrew without merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor and Lingshi plotted in secret. "Liu Jingxuan once marched by Huangwu and came back empty-handed,

sentences.zh: 賊謂我今應從外水往，而料我當出其不意猶從內水來也，必重兵守涪城以備內道。

translations.literal: The bandits will say we should now go by the outer water, yet they will expect us to take them by surprise and still come by the inner water, and will surely mass heavy troops at Fucheng to guard the inner route.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy will expect us on the outer route but fear a surprise strike on the inner water. They will mass troops at Fucheng to block the inner path.

sentences.zh: 若向黃武，正墮其計。

translations.literal: If we go toward Huangwu we will fall right into their plan.
translations.idiomatic: March on Huangwu and we walk straight into their trap.

sentences.zh: 今以大眾自外水取成都，疑兵出內水，此制敵之奇也。

translations.literal: Now with the main force take Chengdu by the outer water while a feint goes by the inner water—this is the marvel of controlling the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Send the main army up the outer water to Chengdu while a feint probes the inner route—that is how we turn their expectations against them."

sentences.zh: 」而慮此聲先馳，賊審虛實，別有函封付齡石，署曰至白帝乃開。

translations.literal: Yet he feared this word would run ahead; the enemy would examine empty and full; he separately sealed another packet for Lingshi, marked to be opened only at Baidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the plan would leak, he sealed a second packet for Lingshi, marked to be opened only at Baidi.

sentences.zh: 諸軍雖進，未知處分，至白帝發書，曰：「眾軍悉從外水取成都；

translations.literal: Though the armies advanced, they did not yet know the disposition; at Baidi the letter was opened, saying, "All armies shall take Chengdu by the outer water;
translations.idiomatic: The columns marched blind until Baidi, where the letter read: "All forces take Chengdu by the outer water;

sentences.zh: 臧熹、朱枚于中水取廣漢；

translations.literal: Zang Xi and Zhu Mei take Guanghan by the middle water;
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi and Zhu Mei take Guanghan by the middle route;

sentences.zh: 使羸弱乘高艦十餘，由內水向黃武。

translations.literal: send weak troops in more than ten high ships by the inner water toward Huangwu."
translations.idiomatic: send a weak detachment in a dozen high-sided ships up the inner water toward Huangwu."

sentences.zh: 」譙縱果備內水，使其大將譙道福戍涪城，遣其秦州刺史侯暉、僕射譙詵等屯彭模，夾水為城。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong indeed prepared the inner water, sent his great general Qiao Daofu to garrison Fucheng, and dispatched his Governor of Qin Hou Hui and Vice Director Qiao Shen and others to camp at Pengmo, building cities on both banks.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Zong did exactly that—garrisoned Fucheng under Daofu, and posted Hou Hui and Qiao Shen at Pengmo with fortified camps on both banks.

sentences.zh: 十年六月，齡石至彭模。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year Lingshi reached Pengmo.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year 10 Lingshi reached Pengmo.

sentences.zh: 七月，齡石率劉鍾、蒯恩等於北城斬侯暉、譙詵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Lingshi led Liu Zhong, Kuai En, and others at the north city and beheaded Hou Hui and Qiao Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he stormed the north wall with Liu Zhong and Kuai En and beheaded Hou Hui and Qiao Shen.

sentences.zh: 朱枚至廣漢，復破譙道福別軍。

translations.literal: Zhu Mei reached Guanghan and again defeated Qiao Daofu's detached army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Mei took Guanghan and routed Daofu's detached force.

sentences.zh: 譙縱奔涪城，巴西人王志斬送之，並獲道福，斬於軍門。

translations.literal: Qiao Zong fled to Fucheng; Wang Zhi of Baxi beheaded and delivered him, and Daofu was also captured and beheaded at the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: Zong fled to Fucheng; Wang Zhi of Baxi cut off his head and sent it in. Daofu was captured and executed at the gate.

sentences.zh: 帝之伐蜀，將謀元帥，乃舉齡石。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to attack Shu and sought a supreme commander, he nominated Lingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Choosing a commander for Shu, the Emperor nominated Lingshi.

sentences.zh: 眾咸謂齡石資名尚輕，慮不克辦，論者甚眾，帝不從。

translations.literal: All said Lingshi's credentials and name were still light, feared he could not succeed, and critics were many; the Emperor did not follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said he was too young and unknown to succeed. The Emperor ignored them.

sentences.zh: 乃分大軍之半，令猛將勁卒悉以配之。

translations.literal: He then divided half the main army and ordered fierce generals and crack troops all assigned to him.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him half the army and every crack unit in the camp.

sentences.zh: 臧熹，敬皇后弟也，亦命受其節度。

translations.literal: Zang Xi, younger brother of the Empress Jing, was also ordered to accept his command.
translations.idiomatic: Even Zang Xi, the Empress Jing's brother, was placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 及戰克捷，眾咸服帝知人，又美齡石善於事。

translations.literal: When battles were won, all submitted that the Emperor knew men, and praised Lingshi's skill in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Victory won universal praise—for the Emperor's eye for talent and Lingshi's command of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 以平蜀功，封豐城侯。

translations.literal: For pacifying Shu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: For conquering Shu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 十四年，桂陽公義真被征，以齡石為雍州刺史，督關中諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the Duke of Guiyang Yizhen was recalled, Lingshi was made Governor of Yong and overseer of all Guanzhong military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14, when Duke of Guiyang Yizhen was recalled, Lingshi became Governor of Yong with command over all Guanzhong forces.

sentences.zh: 齡石至長安，義真乃發。

translations.literal: When Lingshi reached Chang'an, Yizhen then set out.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi reached Chang'an just as Yizhen departed.

sentences.zh: 義真敗於青泥，齡石亦舉城奔走見殺。

translations.literal: Yizhen was defeated at Qingni; Lingshi also abandoned the city and fled and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhen was crushed at Qingni. Lingshi abandoned the city in flight and was killed.

sentences.zh: 傳國至孫，齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: The fief passed to his grandson; when Qi received the abdication the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The title passed to his grandson until Qi abolished the fief.

sentences.zh: 齡石弟超石，亦果銳。

translations.literal: Lingshi's younger brother Chaoshi was also bold and sharp.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chaoshi was equally fierce.

sentences.zh: 雖出自將家，兄弟並閑尺牘。

translations.literal: Though from a general's house, the brothers were both skilled with letters.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers' sons though they were, both brothers were literate men.

sentences.zh: 桓謙為衛將軍，以補行參軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Qian was General of the Guard, Chaoshi was appointed acting staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Qian became General of the Guard, Chaoshi joined his staff.

sentences.zh: 後為武帝徐州主簿，收迎桓謙身首，躬營殯葬。

translations.literal: Later he was chief clerk to the Emperor at Xuzhou, collected and received Huan Qian's head and body, and personally arranged the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as the Emperor's Xuzhou chief clerk, he recovered Huan Qian's body and saw to the burial himself.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年北伐，超石為前鋒入河。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi on the northern expedition, Chaoshi was vanguard entering the river.
translations.idiomatic: On the Yixi 12 northern campaign Chaoshi led the vanguard into the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 時軍人緣河南岸牽百丈。

translations.literal: At the time soldiers along the south bank of the river were hauling hundred-fathom cables.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the south bank were hauling hundred-fathom towlines.

sentences.zh: 有漂度北岸者，輒為魏軍所殺略。

translations.literal: Those who drifted across to the north bank were at once killed and plundered by Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone swept to the north bank was killed or captured by Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝遣白直隊主丁旿率七百人及車百乘于河北岸為卻月陣，兩頭抱河，車置七仗士。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent white-guard squad chief Ding Yu with seven hundred men and a hundred chariots on the north bank in a crescent formation, both ends embracing the river, each chariot carrying seven armed men.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Ding Yu with seven hundred men and a hundred chariots to the north bank in a crescent formation—each chariot holding seven fighters, both wings hugging the river.

sentences.zh: 事畢，使豎一長白毦。

translations.literal: When the work was done he had a long white yak-tail pennant raised.
translations.idiomatic: When the formation was set, a long white yak-tail pennant went up.

sentences.zh: 魏軍不解其意，並未動。

translations.literal: Wei troops did not understand the meaning and all did not move.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army did not understand the signal and held still.

sentences.zh: 帝先命超石戒嚴二千人，白毦既舉，超石赴之，並齎大弩百張，一車益二十人，設彭排於轅上。

translations.literal: The Emperor first ordered Chaoshi to stand two thousand men at alert; once the white pennant was raised Chaoshi rushed to them, all carrying a hundred large crossbows; each chariot gained twenty men, with pengpai shields set on the yoke.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had already put two thousand men on alert under Chaoshi. At the pennant Chaoshi charged in with a hundred heavy crossbows; each chariot took twenty extra men with pengpai shields mounted on the shafts.

sentences.zh: 魏軍見營陣立，乃進圍營。

translations.literal: Wei troops saw the camp formation set and then advanced to surround the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the camp formed, the Wei army closed in to surround it.

sentences.zh: 超石先以弱弓小箭射之，魏軍四面俱至。

translations.literal: Chaoshi first shot them with weak bows and small arrows; Wei troops came from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoshi opened with light bows and small arrows. The Wei closed from every side.

sentences.zh: 魏明元皇帝又遣南平公長孫嵩三萬騎肉薄攻營，於是百弩俱發。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan of Wei also sent the Duke of Nanping, Changsun Song, with thirty thousand cavalry in close assault on the camp; then a hundred crossbows fired together.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan sent Changsun Song, Duke of Nanping, with thirty thousand cavalry in a tight charge. A hundred crossbows loosed at once.

sentences.zh: 魏軍既多，弩不能制，超石初行，別齎大槌並千餘張矟，乃斷矟三四尺以槌槌之，一矟輒洞貫三四人。

translations.literal: Wei troops were many and crossbows could not control them; when Chaoshi first set out he had separately brought large mauls and more than a thousand spears; he broke spears to three or four chi and hammered them—one spear would pierce through three or four men.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy was too many for crossbows alone. Chaoshi had brought great mauls and a thousand spears; he snapped spears to three or four feet and drove them with mauls—each shaft skewered three or four men.

sentences.zh: 魏軍不能當，遂潰。

translations.literal: Wei troops could not withstand it and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei line broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 大軍進克蒲阪，以超石為河東太守。

translations.literal: The main army advanced and took Puban; Chaoshi was made Administrator of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The main army took Puban. Chaoshi was made Administrator of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 後除中書侍郎，封興平縣五等侯。

translations.literal: Later he was removed to Palace Secretariat Gentleman and enfeoffed as Fifth-Rank Marquis of Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Palace Secretariat Gentleman and enfeoffed as fifth-rank Marquis of Xingping.

sentences.zh: 關中亂，帝遣超石慰勞河洛，與齡石俱沒赫連勃勃，見殺。

translations.literal: When Guanzhong fell into disorder the Emperor sent Chaoshi to comfort the He-Luo region; he and Lingshi both perished before Helian Bobo and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanzhong collapsed the Emperor sent Chaoshi to steady the He-Luo region. He and Lingshi both fell to Helian Bobo and were killed.

sentences.zh: 毛修之字敬文，滎陽陽武人也。

translations.literal: Mao Xiuzhi, styled Jingwen, was a man of Yangwu in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi, styled Jingwen, came from Yangwu in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 祖武生、伯父璩並益州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wusheng and father's elder brother Qu were both Governors of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wusheng and uncle Qu had both governed Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 父瑾，梁、秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jin was Governor of Liang and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jin had governed Liang and Qin.

sentences.zh: 修之仕桓玄為屯騎校尉，隨玄西奔。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi served Huan Xuan as Colonel of the Resolute Cavalry and followed Xuan fleeing west.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi served Huan Xuan as Colonel of Resolute Cavalry and fled west with him.

sentences.zh: 玄欲奔漢川，修之誘令入蜀。

translations.literal: Xuan wished to flee to Hanzhong; Xiuzhi induced him to enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan meant to flee to Hanzhong; Xiuzhi steered him into Shu instead.

sentences.zh: 馮遷斬玄於枚洄洲，修之力也。

translations.literal: Feng Qian beheaded Xuan at Meihui Isle—Xiuzhi's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Qian killed Xuan at Meihui Isle—Xiuzhi's work.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝以為鎮軍諮議，遷右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song made him advisory officer of the Pacifying Army and transferred him to General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu made him Pacifying Army adviser, then General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 既有斬玄之謀，又父伯並在蜀，帝欲引為外助，故頻加榮爵。

translations.literal: Since he had plotted to kill Xuan and both his father and uncles were in Shu, the Emperor wished to draw him as outside aid and therefore repeatedly added honors and fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: He had plotted Xuan's death, and his father and uncles still lived in Shu. The Emperor courted him as an outside ally and heaped honors on him.

sentences.zh: 及父瑾為譙縱所殺，帝表修之為龍驤將軍，配兵遣奔赴。

translations.literal: When his father Jin was killed by Qiao Zong, the Emperor memorialized making Xiuzhi General of Dragon Valor, assigned troops, and sent him in haste.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiao Zong killed his father Jin, the Emperor made Xiuzhi Dragon Valor general, gave him troops, and sent him west at once.

sentences.zh: 時益州刺史鮑陋不肯進討，修之言狀，帝乃令冠軍將軍劉敬宣伐蜀，無功而退。

translations.literal: At the time Governor of Yizhou Bao Lou would not advance to attack; Xiuzhi reported the situation, and the Emperor then ordered Champion General Liu Jingxuan to attack Shu; without merit he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Bao Lou refused to march. Xiuzhi reported it, and the Emperor sent Liu Jingxuan against Shu—but Jingxuan came back empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 譙縱由此送修之父伯及中表喪柩口累並得還。

translations.literal: Because of this Qiao Zong sent back Xiuzhi's father, uncles, and the coffins of kin by marriage, all obtained return.
translations.idiomatic: Through this Qiao Zong returned Xiuzhi's father, uncles, and the coffins of his kin.

sentences.zh: 後劉毅西鎮江陵，以為衛軍司馬、南郡太守。

translations.literal: Later Liu Yi garrisoned the west at Jiangling and made Xiuzhi Staff Major of the Guard Army and Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liu Yi garrisoned Jiangling and made Xiuzhi Guard Army staff major and Administrator of Nan.

sentences.zh: 修之雖為毅將佐，而深結於帝，及毅敗見宥。

translations.literal: Though Xiuzhi was Yi's staff officer, he was deeply tied to the Emperor; when Yi fell he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served Liu Yi, he was secretly loyal to the Emperor and was spared when Yi fell.

sentences.zh: 時遣朱齡石伐蜀，修之固求行。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Lingshi was sent to attack Shu; Xiuzhi firmly begged to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Lingshi marched on Shu, Xiuzhi begged to go along.

sentences.zh: 帝慮修之至蜀多所誅殺，且土人既與毛氏有嫌，亦當以死自固。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared that if Xiuzhi reached Shu he would kill many, and that since the locals already bore grudges against the Mao clan they would also fight to the death to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor feared Xiuzhi would slaughter his way through Shu, and that locals who hated the Maos would fight to the death against him.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: He did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 修之不信鬼神，所至必焚房廟。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi did not believe in ghosts and spirits; wherever he went he always burned temples.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi scorned gods and burned every temple he passed.

sentences.zh: 時蔣山廟中有好牛馬，並奪取之。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangshan temple had fine cattle and horses; he seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Jiangshan Temple of its best cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 累遷相國右司馬，行司州事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Major of the Chancellor's staff, acting Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Major on the chancellor's staff, acting Governor of Si.

sentences.zh: 戍洛陽，修立城壘。

translations.literal: Garrisoning Luoyang, he repaired city walls and forts.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisoning Luoyang, he rebuilt walls and fortifications.

sentences.zh: 武帝至，履行善之，賜衣服玩好，當時評直二千萬。

translations.literal: When the Emperor arrived he inspected and approved, bestowed clothes and fine objects worth twenty million at current valuation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor inspected his work, approved it, and gave gifts worth twenty million by current reckoning.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡死，修之代為安西司馬。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhen'e died, Xiuzhi replaced him as Pacifying West staff major.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Zhen'e's death Xiuzhi replaced him as Pacifying West staff major.

sentences.zh: 桂陽公義真敗，為赫連勃勃所禽。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Guiyang Yizhen was defeated he was captured by Helian Bobo.
translations.idiomatic: When Duke of Guiyang Yizhen was defeated, Helian Bobo took him captive.

sentences.zh: 及赫連昌滅，入魏。

translations.literal: When Helian Chang was destroyed he entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Helian Chang fell, Xiuzhi passed into Wei.

sentences.zh: 修之在洛，敬事嵩高道士寇謙之。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi at Luoyang reverently served Songgao Daoist Kou Qianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang Xiuzhi became a devotee of the Daoist Kou Qianzhi of Songgao.

sentences.zh: 謙之為魏太武帝信敬，營護之，故不死。

translations.literal: Qianzhi was trusted and honored by Emperor Taiwu of Wei and protected him, so he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhi enjoyed Taiwu's trust and shielded him, so he survived.

sentences.zh: 修之嘗為羊羹薦魏尚書，尚書以為絕味，獻之太武，大悅，以為太官令，被寵，遂為尚書、光祿大夫，封南郡公，太官令、尚書如故。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi once made mutton soup and presented it to a Wei minister; the minister thought it supreme flavor and presented it to Taiwu, who was greatly pleased and made him Director of the Imperial Kitchen, favored; he then became Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Marquis of Nan commandery, keeping the posts of Director of the Imperial Kitchen and Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He once served mutton soup to a Wei minister who found it exquisite and sent it to Taiwu. Delighted, the emperor made him Director of the Imperial Kitchen, then Minister, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Marquis of Nan—keeping both kitchen and ministerial posts.

sentences.zh: 後朱修之俘于魏亦見寵，修之問朱修之，南國當權者為誰，答云殷景仁。

translations.literal: Later when Zhu Xiuzhi was captured in Wei he too was favored; Xiuzhi asked Zhu Xiuzhi who held power in the southern state; he answered Yin Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhu Xiuzhi, also a Wei captive, rose in favor. Mao Xiuzhi asked who held power in the south. Zhu Xiuzhi answered: Yin Jingren.

sentences.zh: 修之笑曰：「吾昔在南，殷尚幼少，我歸罪之日，便當巾韝到門。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi laughed and said, "In old days in the south Yin was still very young; on the day I return in disgrace I shall go straight to his door with headcloth and bridle."
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi laughed. "When I left the south Yin was a boy. The day I crawl home in shame I'll show up at his gate with bridle in hand."

sentences.zh: 」經年不忍問家消息，久之乃訪焉。

translations.literal: For years he could not bear to ask news of his family; only after long time did he inquire.
translations.idiomatic: For years he could not bring himself to ask after his family. Only much later did he inquire.

sentences.zh: 修之具答，並云：「賢子元矯甚能自處。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi answered fully and also said, "Your worthy son Yuanjiao manages himself very well."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi told him everything and added, "Your worthy son Yuanjiao is managing well."

sentences.zh: 」修之悲不得言，直視良久，乃長歎曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: Xiuzhi grieved and could not speak; he stared straight ahead a long time, then sighed deeply, "Alas!"
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiuzhi could not speak for grief. He stared a long while, then sighed, "Ah!"

sentences.zh: 」自此一不復及。

translations.literal: From this he never spoke of it again.
translations.idiomatic: He never raised the subject again.

sentences.zh: 初，北人去來言修之勸魏侵邊，並教以在南禮制，文帝甚疑責之。

translations.literal: At first northerners coming and going said Xiuzhi urged Wei to invade the border and also taught southern ritual institutions; Emperor Wen greatly suspected and blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: At first travelers from the north claimed Xiuzhi had urged Wei to raid the frontier and taught them southern court ritual. Emperor Wen suspected him deeply.

sentences.zh: 朱修之後得還，具相申理，上意乃釋。

translations.literal: When Zhu Xiuzhi later returned he fully explained and cleared the matter; the Emperor's mind was then released.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Xiuzhi returned south he cleared the matter fully, and the emperor's suspicions lifted.

sentences.zh: 修之在魏多妻妾，男女甚眾，身遂死于魏。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi in Wei had many wives and concubines and many sons and daughters; he finally died in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi took many wives in Wei, fathered many children, and died there.

sentences.zh: 孫惠素，仕齊為少府卿。

translations.literal: His grandson Huisu served Qi as Director of the Palace Parks.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Huisu served Qi as Director of the Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，母服除後，更修母所住處床帳屏帷，每月朔十五向帷悲泣，傍人為之感傷，終身如此。

translations.literal: His nature was utmost filial; after his mother's mourning period ended he again repaired the bed, curtains, and screens of his mother's dwelling; on the first and fifteenth of each month he wept toward the curtains, and bystanders were moved to sorrow; he did this all his life.
translations.idiomatic: Huisu was profoundly filial. After his mourning ended he kept his mother's bed and curtains as she had left them, and on the first and fifteenth of every month he wept before them until onlookers wept too—for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 惠素吏才強濟，而臨事清刻，敕市銅官碧青一千二百斤供禦畫，用錢六十五萬。

translations.literal: Huisu was strong in administrative talent yet stern and exacting in affairs; he was ordered to purchase twelve hundred jin of imperial green malachite from the copper office for court painting, using six hundred fifty thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Huisu was a capable administrator but harsh in office. Ordered to buy twelve hundred jin of malachite for court painting, he spent six hundred fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 有讒惠素納利，武帝怒，敕尚書評價，貴二十八萬餘，有司奏，伏誅。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Huisu for taking profit; Emperor Wu was angry and ordered the Ministry to assess price, valuing it at more than two hundred eighty thousand excess; the relevant office memorialized and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: A slanderer accused him of profiteering. Emperor Wu ordered a price review that found an excess of two hundred eighty thousand. He was executed on memorial.

sentences.zh: 死後家徒四壁，武帝后知無罪，甚悔恨之。

translations.literal: After death his house had only bare walls; the Empress later learned he was innocent and deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He died leaving only bare walls. The empress later learned he was innocent and was deeply remorseful.

sentences.zh: 傅弘之字仲度，北地泥陽人也。

translations.literal: Fu Hongzhi, styled Zhongdu, was a man of Niyang in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hongzhi, styled Zhongdu, came from Niyang in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 傅氏舊屬靈州，漢末失土，寄馮翊，置泥陽、富平二縣，廢靈州，故傅氏悉屬泥陽。

translations.literal: The Fu clan originally belonged to Lingzhou; at the end of Han they lost their lands, lodged in Fengyi, established the counties of Niyang and Fuping, abolished Lingzhou, so the Fu clan all belonged to Niyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Fu clan had originally held Lingzhou. At the end of Han they lost their lands, resettled in Fengyi, and were registered at Niyang and Fuping when Lingzhou was abolished.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康三年復立靈州縣，傅氏還屬靈州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taikang of Emperor Wu of Jin Lingzhou county was restored; the Fu clan returned to belonging to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Taikang year 3 Lingzhou was restored and the Fu clan was re-registered there.

sentences.zh: 弘之高祖祗，晉司徒，後封靈州公。

translations.literal: Hongzhi's great-grandfather Di was Jin Minister Over the Masses, later enfeoffed as Duke of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi's great-grandfather Di had been Jin Minister Over the Masses and was later enfeoffed Duke of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 不欲封本縣，故祗一門還屬泥陽。

translations.literal: Not wishing to be enfeoffed in his home county, therefore only Di's household returned to belonging to Niyang.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to hold a fief in his native county, only Di's branch remained registered at Niyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖暢，秘書丞，沒石勒，生子洪。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Chang was Secretariat Director, captured by Shi Le, and bore Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Chang, a Secretariat Director, was captured by Shi Le and fathered Hong.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝永和中，石氏亂，度江。

translations.literal: In the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin the Shi clan fell into disorder and he crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Mu's Yonghe era, when the Shi regime collapsed, Hong crossed south over the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 洪生梁州刺史歆，歆生弘之。

translations.literal: Hong bore Governor of Liang Xin; Xin bore Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's son Xin governed Liang; Xin's son was Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻有大志，歷位太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: In youth he was free-spirited with great ambition and held the post of acting staff officer to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and ambitious, serving as acting staff officer to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝北伐，弘之與扶風太守沈田子等七軍自武關入。

translations.literal: On Emperor Wu's northern expedition Hongzhi and Administrator of Fufeng Shen Tianzi with seven armies entered by Wuguan.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern expedition Hongzhi entered through Wuguan with Shen Tianzi of Fufeng and seven columns.

sentences.zh: 弘之素習騎乘，于姚泓馳道內戲馬，甚有姿制，羌胡觀者數千，並歎稱善。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was skilled in riding from old habit; within Yao Hong's imperial road he played at horsemanship with great grace; several thousand Qiang and Hu onlookers all sighed and praised his skill.
translations.idiomatic: A lifelong rider, he raced horses on Yao Hong's imperial track with superb style. Thousands of Qiang and Hu spectators sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 留為桂陽公義真雍州中從事史。

translations.literal: He was retained as Central Attendant Clerk of Yong Province under the Duke of Guiyang Yizhen.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed on as Central Attendant Clerk of Yong under Duke of Guiyang Yizhen.

sentences.zh: 及義真東歸，赫連勃勃傾國追躡，於青泥大戰，弘之躬貫甲胄，氣冠三軍，軍敗陷沒，不為之屈。

translations.literal: When Yizhen returned east, Helian Bobo with all the nation's strength pursued; at Qingni they fought a great battle; Hongzhi personally donned armor, his spirit topping the three armies; the army was defeated and he was captured, yet he did not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Yizhen marched east, Helian Bobo pursued with the full strength of his state. At Qingni they fought a great battle. Hongzhi armored himself and his spirit outshone the whole army. Defeated and captured, he still would not yield.

sentences.zh: 時天大寒裸弘之，弘之叫駡見殺。

translations.literal: At the time the sky was bitterly cold and they stripped Hongzhi naked; Hongzhi cursed and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: It was bitter cold. They stripped him naked. He cursed them and was killed.

sentences.zh: 朱修之字恭祖，義陽平氏人也。

translations.literal: Zhu Xiuzhi, styled Gongzu, was a man of Pingshi in Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi, styled Gongzu, came from Pingshi in Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 曾祖燾，晉平西將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tao was Jin General Pacifying the West.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tao had been Jin's General Pacifying the West.

sentences.zh: 祖序，豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xu was Governor of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xu had governed Yu.

sentences.zh: 父諶，益州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Chen was Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chen had governed Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 修之初為州主簿，宋元嘉中，累遷司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi at first was provincial chief clerk; in the Yuanjia era he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi began as a provincial chief clerk and in the Yuanjia era rose to Attendant Gentleman of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 文帝謂曰：「卿曾祖昔為王導丞相中郎，卿今又為王弘中郎，可謂不忝爾祖矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen told him, "Your great-grandfather once served Wang Dao as chief clerk in the chancellor's office; you now serve Wang Hong as chief clerk—you may be said not to disgrace your ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told him, "Your great-grandfather served Wang Dao as the chancellor's chief clerk; you now serve Wang Hong in the same post. You honor your line."

sentences.zh: 後隨右軍到彥之北侵，彥之自河南回，修之留戍滑台，被魏將安頡攻圍。

translations.literal: Later he followed the Right Army Dao Yanzhi on a northern raid; Yanzhi returned from south of the river; Xiuzhi remained to garrison Huatai and was besieged by Wei General An Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Dao Yanzhi's Right Army on a northern raid. When Yanzhi withdrew south of the river, Xiuzhi stayed to hold Huatai and was besieged by Wei's An Ji.

sentences.zh: 糧盡，將士熏鼠食之。

translations.literal: Grain was exhausted; officers and soldiers smoked rats to eat them.
translations.idiomatic: Food ran out. The garrison smoked rats for meat.

sentences.zh: 修之被圍既久，母常悲憂，忽一旦乳汁驚出，母號慟告家人曰：「我年老非復有乳汁時，今如此，兒必沒矣。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi had been besieged long; his mother was often sorrowful; suddenly one day milk burst out in shock; his mother wailed and told the family, "I am old and no longer of the age for milk; now this happens—my son is surely lost."
translations.idiomatic: His mother grieved through the long siege. One day her milk burst out in shock. She wailed to the family, "I am too old for milk—if this happens, my son is dead."

sentences.zh: 」魏果以其日克滑台，囚之。

translations.literal: Wei indeed on that day took Huatai and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took Huatai that very day and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太武嘉其固守之節，以為雲中鎮將，妻以宗室女。

translations.literal: Taiwu praised his steadfast defense and made him garrison general of Yunzhong, giving him an imperial-clan woman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu honored his stubborn defense, made him garrison general of Yunzhong, and gave him an imperial-clan bride.

sentences.zh: 修之潛謀南歸，妻疑之，每流涕謂曰：「觀敘無停意，何不告我以實，義不相負。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi secretly plotted return south; his wife suspected him and wept each time, saying, "I see your restlessness without pause—why not tell me the truth? I will not fail you in righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: He plotted escape south. His wife suspected him and wept, "You never sit still—tell me the truth. I will not betray you."

sentences.zh: 」修之深嘉其義而不告也。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi deeply admired her righteousness yet did not tell her.
translations.idiomatic: He admired her loyalty but told her nothing.

sentences.zh: 及太武伐馮弘，修之及同沒人邢懷明並從。

translations.literal: When Taiwu attacked Feng Hong, Xiuzhi and fellow captive Xing Huaiming both followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu attacked Feng Hong, Xiuzhi and fellow captive Xing Huaiming marched with the army.

sentences.zh: 又有徐卓者亦沒魏，復欲率南人竊發，事泄見誅。

translations.literal: There was also Xu Zhuo, also captive in Wei, who again wished to lead southerners in a secret rising; the affair leaked and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Another captive, Xu Zhuo, tried to lead southerners in a secret uprising. The plot leaked and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 修之、懷明懼禍，同奔馮弘，不見禮。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi and Huaiming feared disaster and fled together to Feng Hong, and were not treated with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi and Huaiming fled to Feng Hong in fear. They were not welcomed.

sentences.zh: 停一年，會宋使至。

translations.literal: They stayed one year; then a Song envoy arrived.
translations.idiomatic: They lingered a year until a Song envoy arrived.

sentences.zh: 修之名位素顯，傳詔見便拜。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's name and rank had always been prominent; seeing the imperial messenger he at once bowed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's name was well known. At sight of the imperial messenger he bowed at once.

sentences.zh: 彼國敬傳詔，呼為天子邊人。

translations.literal: That country respected the imperial messenger and called him the emperor's frontier man.
translations.idiomatic: The northerners honored the envoy and called him the emperor's man from the frontier.

sentences.zh: 見傳詔致敬，乃始禮之。

translations.literal: Seeing the messenger pay respect, they then began to treat Xiuzhi with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they saw the envoy's courtesy did they begin to treat Xiuzhi with respect.

sentences.zh: 時魏屢伐黃龍，弘遣使求救，修之乃使傳詔說而遣之。

translations.literal: At the time Wei repeatedly attacked Huanglong; Hong sent envoys begging rescue; Xiuzhi then had the messenger persuade and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was hammering Huanglong. Feng Hong sent envoys begging aid. Xiuzhi had the Song messenger talk them into leaving.

sentences.zh: 泛海，未至東萊，舫柂折，風猛，海師慮向海北，垂長索，舫乃正。

translations.literal: They sailed the sea; before reaching Donglai the boat's rudder broke; the wind was fierce; the sailors feared drifting north; they lowered a long rope and the boat then straightened.
translations.idiomatic: They sailed east. Before Donglai the rudder snapped in a fierce wind. Sailors feared drifting north until a long rope righted the hull.

sentences.zh: 海師視上有鳥飛，知去岸不遠，須臾至東萊。

translations.literal: The sailors saw birds flying above and knew land was not far; in a moment they reached Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Birds overhead told the sailors land was near. Moments later they made Donglai.

sentences.zh: 及至，以為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: On arrival he was made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，累遷甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu he was repeatedly promoted to Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians and Governor of Yong, with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he rose to Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians and Governor of Yong with full military command.

sentences.zh: 修之政在寬簡，士庶悅附。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's governance was lenient and simple; gentry and commoners gladly attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and plain. Gentry and commoners alike rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 及荊州刺史南郡王義宣反，檄修之舉兵。

translations.literal: When Governor of Jing and Prince of Nan commandery Yixuan rebelled, he sent a proclamation summoning Xiuzhi to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Nan commandery Yixuan rebelled as Governor of Jing, he summoned Xiuzhi to join.

sentences.zh: 雍土時饑，修之偽與之同；

translations.literal: Yong province was then in famine; Xiuzhi feigned agreement with him;
translations.idiomatic: Yong was starving. Xiuzhi pretended to agree;

sentences.zh: 既而遣使陳情于孝武，孝武嘉之，以為荊州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: presently he sent an envoy to state his loyalty to Xiaowu; Xiaowu praised this and made him Governor of Jing with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: then sent an envoy pledging loyalty to Xiaowu, who rewarded him with the governorship of Jing and full command.

sentences.zh: 義宣乃聞修之不同，更以魯秀為雍州刺史，擊襄陽。

translations.literal: Yixuan then learned Xiuzhi would not join and instead made Lu Xiu Governor of Yong and attacked Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Xiuzhi would not join, Yixuan made Lu Xiu Governor of Yong and struck at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 修之命斷馬鞍山道，秀不得前乃退。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi ordered Ma'an Mountain road cut; Xiu could not advance and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi blocked the Ma'an Mountain road. Xiu could not advance and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 修之率眾向江陵，竺超已執義宣，修之至，於獄殺之。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi led the masses toward Jiangling; Zhu Chao had already seized Yixuan; when Xiuzhi arrived he killed Yixuan in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi marched on Jiangling. Zhu Chao had already taken Yixuan. Xiuzhi arrived and executed him in prison.

sentences.zh: 以功封南昌縣侯。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was enfeoffed Marquis of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 修之立身清約，百城貺贈，一無所受。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi in conduct was pure and frugal; gifts from a hundred cities he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He lived cleanly and frugally and refused gifts from every city in his province.

sentences.zh: 唯以蠻人宜存撫納，有餉皆受，得輒與佐史賭之，未嘗入己。

translations.literal: Only because barbarians should be soothed and won he accepted all offerings, and once received he at once gambled them with staff officers, never keeping them for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Only barbarian tribute did he accept—for diplomacy's sake—and he gambled every coin away with his staff, keeping nothing.

sentences.zh: 去鎮之日，秋毫無犯。

translations.literal: On the day he left his post not the slightest thing was violated.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office not a hair of public property was missing.

sentences.zh: 計在州以來，然油及私牛馬食官穀草，以私錢六十萬償之。

translations.literal: He calculated from his time in the province: lamp oil and private cattle and horses eating official grain and fodder—he repaid with private cash six hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He reckoned every lamp drop of oil and every mouthful of fodder his private stock had consumed, and repaid six hundred thousand in private cash.

sentences.zh: 而儉刻無潤，薄于恩情，姊在鄉里，饑寒不立，修之貴為刺史，未曾供贍。

translations.literal: Yet he was harsh and ungenerous, thin in affection; his elder sister in the countryside could not support herself in hunger and cold; though Xiuzhi was exalted as governor he never supplied her.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was harsh and stingy with kin. His elder sister lived in poverty in the countryside; though he was a governor he never sent her aid.

sentences.zh: 往姊家，姊為設菜羹粗飯以激之，修之曰：「此是貧家好食，進之致飽。

translations.literal: Going to his sister's house, his sister set out vegetable soup and coarse rice to provoke him; Xiuzhi said, "This is poor people's good food—I eat my fill and advance it."
translations.idiomatic: Visiting her, she served only vegetable broth and coarse rice to shame him. He said, "Poor folk's fare—I'll eat my fill and be grateful."

sentences.zh: 」先是，新野庾彥達為益州刺史，攜姊之鎮，資給供奉，中分秩祿，西土稱焉。

translations.literal: Before this, Yu Yanda of Xinye as Governor of Yizhou brought his sister to the post, supplied and maintained her, sharing half his salary; the western lands praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Before him Yu Yanda of Xinye had brought his sister to Yizhou, shared half his salary, and was praised throughout the west.

sentences.zh: 修之後拜左戶尚書、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was later made Left Minister of the Household and General of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Left Minister of the Household and General of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 至建鄴，牛奔墜車折腳，辭尚書，徙崇憲太僕，仍加特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Reaching Jiankang his ox bolted, he fell from the cart and broke his leg; he resigned the ministry and was transferred to Grand Master of Chongxian, still given special advancement and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiankang his ox bolted and broke his leg. He resigned the ministry for Grand Master of Chongxian, with special advancement and the gold seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 腳疾不堪獨行見，特給扶侍。

translations.literal: His leg ailment could not bear walking alone to audience; he was specially given attendants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: His leg would not bear walking to court alone; he was granted attendants to lean on.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡貞侯。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Zhen Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He died with the posthumous name Zhen Marquis.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨字彥德，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo, styled Yande, was a man of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo, styled Yande, came from Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六世祖宏，河東太守、綿竹侯，以從叔司徒允之難，棄官北居新興，仍為新興、雁門太守。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Hong was Administrator of Hedong and Marquis of Mianzhu; because of following his father's younger brother Minister Xu in hardship he abandoned office and went north to live in Xinxing, and still served as Administrator of Xinxing and Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations back, Hong was Administrator of Hedong and Marquis of Mianzhu. Following his uncle Minister Xu into exile he abandoned office, moved north to Xinxing, and governed Xinxing and Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 其自序云爾。

translations.literal: His self-written genealogy says so.
translations.idiomatic: So his family genealogy records.

sentences.zh: 祖牢，仕慕容氏為上谷太守，隨慕容德居青州。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lao served the Murong clan as Administrator of Shanggu and followed Murong De to dwell in Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lao served the Murong as Administrator of Shanggu and followed Murong De to Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 父秀，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Xiu died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiu died young.

sentences.zh: 玄謨幼而不群，世父蕤有知人鑒，常笑曰：「此兒氣概高亮，有太尉彥雲之風。

translations.literal: Xuanmo in youth was unlike others; his father's elder brother Rui had knowledge of men and often laughed, saying, "This boy's spirit is lofty and bright, with the air of Grand Commandant Yan Yun."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Xuanmo stood apart. His uncle Rui, who read men well, laughed and said, "This child has the lofty bearing of Grand Commandant Yan Yun."

sentences.zh: 」宋武帝臨徐州，辟為從事史，與語異之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song was at Xuzhou he summoned him as staff officer and in speaking found him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu held Xuzhou he summoned Xuanmo to his staff and was struck by him in conversation.

sentences.zh: 少帝末，謝晦為荊州，請為南蠻行參軍、武甯太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Shaodi's reign Xie Hui was in Jing Province and requested him as acting staff officer of the Southern Barbarians and Administrator of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shaodi's reign Xie Hui governed Jing and made him acting Southern Barbarians staff officer and Administrator of Wuning.

sentences.zh: 晦敗，以非大帥見原。

translations.literal: When Hui fell he was pardoned because he was not the chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui fell he was spared because he had not been the chief conspirator.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，補長沙王義欣鎮軍中兵參軍，領汝陰太守。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he was appointed staff major of the Pacifying Army under Prince of Changsha Yixin, and Administrator of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia he became Pacifying Army staff major to Prince of Changsha Yixin and Administrator of Runan.

sentences.zh: 每陳北侵之規，上謂殷景仁曰：「聞王玄謨陳說，使人有封狼居胥意。」

translations.literal: Each time he presented plans for northern invasion the Emperor told Yin Jingren, "When I hear Wang Xuanmo's proposals I feel the will to seal Wolf Mountain."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he urged a northern campaign the Emperor told Yin Jingren, "Hearing Xuanmo speak, I feel like planting my banner on Wolf Mountain."

sentences.zh: 後為興安侯義賓輔國司馬、彭城太守。

translations.literal: Later he was Pacifying State staff major to the Marquis of Xing'an Yibin and Administrator of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Pacifying State staff major to Marquis of Xing'an Yibin and Administrator of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 義賓薨，玄謨上表，以彭城要兼水陸，請以皇子撫臨州政，乃以孝武出鎮。

translations.literal: When Yibin died Xuanmo memorialized that Pengcheng was strategically vital on land and water and asked that a prince oversee the province; thus Xiaowu was sent to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yibin died Xuanmo argued that Pengcheng commanded land and water routes and begged a prince to govern it. Xiaowu was sent to garrison the post.

sentences.zh: 及大舉北侵，以玄謨為甯朔將軍。

translations.literal: When the great northern invasion was launched Xuanmo was made General Pacifying the North.
translations.idiomatic: On the great northern campaign Xuanmo was made General Pacifying the North.

sentences.zh: 前鋒入河，受輔國將軍蕭斌節度。

translations.literal: The vanguard entered the river and accepted the command of Pacifying State General Xiao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard entered the Yellow River under Pacifying State General Xiao Bin.

sentences.zh: 軍至碻磝，玄謨進向滑台，圍城二百餘日。

translations.literal: The army reached Queqiu; Xuanmo advanced toward Huatai and besieged the city more than two hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Queqiu. Xuanmo pushed on to Huatai and besieged it for more than two hundred days.

sentences.zh: 魏太武自來救之，眾號百萬，鼓鞞動天地。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu of Wei came in person to rescue; the host was said to number a million; drums and flails shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu came in person with an army said to number a million. Drums and war-flails shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 玄謨之行也，眾力不少，器械精嚴，而專仗所見，多行殺戮。

translations.literal: When Xuanmo marched his force was not small and equipment was fine and strict, yet he relied solely on what he saw and often carried out killings.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo's column was strong and well equipped, yet he governed by whim and slaughtered freely.

sentences.zh: 初圍城，城內多茅屋，眾求以火箭燒之。
