translations.literal: At first besieging the city, inside were many thatched houses; the troops asked to burn them with fire arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the walls were many thatched houses. The men asked to burn them with fire arrows.

sentences.zh: 玄謨曰：「損亡軍實。

translations.literal: Xuanmo said, "That would destroy army stores."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo refused: "That wastes our plunder."

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 城中即撤壞之，穴地為窟室。

translations.literal: Inside the city they at once tore them down and dug earth into cave rooms.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders tore the thatch down and dug underground shelters.

sentences.zh: 及魏救將至，眾請發車為營，又不從。

translations.literal: When Wei's rescue was about to arrive the troops asked to deploy chariots as camp; again he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei's relief approached the men asked to form chariot fortifications. Again he refused.

sentences.zh: 將士並懷離怨。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers all harbored alienation and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers alike turned resentful.

sentences.zh: 又營貨利，一匹布責人八百梨，以此倍失人心。

translations.literal: He also traded for profit—one bolt of cloth he charged eight hundred pears—and by this doubly lost men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He also profiteered—one bolt of cloth for eight hundred pears—and lost hearts twice over.

sentences.zh: 及太武軍至，乃夜遁，麾下散亡略盡。

translations.literal: When Taiwu's army arrived he fled by night; those under his command scattered and fled, nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiwu arrived he fled by night. His command scattered until almost none remained.

sentences.zh: 蕭斌將斬之，沈慶之固諫曰：「佛狸威震天下，控弦百萬，豈玄謨所能當。

translations.literal: Xiao Bin was about to behead him; Shen Qingzhi firmly remonstrated, saying, "Bili's might shakes the world; he controls a million bowstrings—how can Xuanmo withstand him?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bin meant to execute him. Shen Qingzhi protested firmly: "Bili's power shakes the world. A million bows answer his call—Xuanmo was never meant to stand alone against that.

sentences.zh: 殺戰將以自弱，非良計也。

translations.literal: Killing a battle general to weaken oneself is no good plan."
translations.idiomatic: Beheading your own general only weakens you. That is no strategy."

sentences.zh: 」斌乃止。

translations.literal: Bin then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Bin stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 初，玄謨始將見殺，夢人告曰：「誦觀世音千遍則免。

translations.literal: At first when Xuanmo was about to be killed he dreamed a man told him, "Recite Guanyin a thousand times and you will be spared."
translations.idiomatic: When execution seemed certain Xuanmo dreamed a voice saying, "Chant to Guanyin a thousand times and you will live."

sentences.zh: 」玄謨夢中曰：「何可竟也。

translations.literal: Xuanmo said in the dream, "How can one finish that?"
translations.idiomatic: In the dream he answered, "Who could finish a thousand?"

sentences.zh: 」仍見授，既覺誦之，且得千遍。

translations.literal: He was still given the text; once awake he recited it and reached a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the text was placed in his hands. Awake, he chanted until he reached a thousand.

sentences.zh: 明日將刑，誦之不輟。

translations.literal: The next day as execution approached he did not stop reciting.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, facing execution, he never stopped chanting.

sentences.zh: 忽傳唱停刑，遣代守碻磝。

translations.literal: Suddenly came word to halt execution; he was sent to replace the garrison at Queqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly an order halted the execution and sent him to hold Queqiu instead.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭為征討都督，以碻磝沙城不可守，召令還。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong was supreme commander of the punitive campaign; because Queqiu's sand walls could not be held he summoned him to return.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong commanded the punitive expedition. Judging Queqiu's sand walls untenable, he recalled Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 為魏軍所追，大破之，流矢中臂。

translations.literal: Wei troops pursued and routed them greatly; a stray arrow struck his arm.
translations.idiomatic: Wei pursuers routed the column. A stray arrow struck his arm.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，還至曆城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year he returned to Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 28 he returned to Licheng.

sentences.zh: 義恭與玄謨書曰：「聞因敗為成，臂上金創，將非金印之征邪？」

translations.literal: Yigong wrote to Xuanmo, "I hear that from defeat comes victory and a golden wound on the arm—is this not the sign of a golden seal?"
translations.idiomatic: Yigong wrote him, "They say defeat turns to victory and a golden wound on the arm foretells a golden seal."

sentences.zh: 元凶弑立，以玄謨為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince usurped and established himself Xuanmo was made Governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince murdered his way to the throne Xuanmo was made Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 孝武伐逆，玄謨遣濟南太守垣護之等將兵赴義。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu marched against the usurper Xuanmo sent Administrator of Jinan Yuan Huzhi and others with troops to join the righteous cause.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu marched against the usurper Xuanmo sent Yuan Huzhi of Jinan and others to join the loyal side.

sentences.zh: 事平，除徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was made Governor of Xuzhou with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he became Governor of Xuzhou with full command.

sentences.zh: 及南郡王義宣與江州刺史臧質反，朝廷假玄謨輔國將軍，為前鋒南討，拜豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Prince of Nan commandery Yixuan and Governor of Jiangzhou Zang Zhi rebelled, the court made Xuanmo acting Pacifying State General as vanguard for the southern punitive campaign and appointed him Governor of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixuan and Zang Zhi of Jiangzhou rebelled, the court made Xuanmo acting Pacifying State General, southern vanguard, and Governor of Yu.

sentences.zh: 質尋至，大破之。

translations.literal: When Zhi arrived he was routed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi came up Xuanmo crushed him.

sentences.zh: 加都督，封曲江縣侯。

translations.literal: He was given added overall command and enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He received full command and the marquisate of Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 中軍司馬劉沖之白孝武，言玄謨在梁山與義宣通謀。

translations.literal: Central Army Staff Major Liu Chongzhi reported to Xiaowu that at Liangshan Xuanmo had secretly plotted with Yixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Major Liu Chongzhi told Xiaowu that at Liangshan Xuanmo had secretly colluded with Yixuan.

sentences.zh: 檢雖無實，上意不能明，使有司奏玄謨沒匿所得賊寶物，虛張戰簿，與徐州刺史垣護之並免官。

translations.literal: Though the investigation found no proof, the Emperor's mind could not be cleared; he had the relevant office memorialize that Xuanmo concealed captured rebel goods, falsified battle records, and together with Governor of Xuzhou Yuan Huzhi was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The inquiry found nothing, yet the emperor's doubt lingered. Officials memorialized that Xuanmo had hidden loot and falsified battle rolls. He and Yuan Huzhi were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋為甯蠻校尉、雍州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians and Governor of Yong with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as Colonel Pacifying the Barbarians and Governor of Yong with full command.

sentences.zh: 雍土多諸僑寓，玄謨上言所統僑郡無有境土，新舊錯亂，租課不時，宜加併合。

translations.literal: Yong had many migrant settlements; Xuanmo memorialized that the migrant commanderies under his command had no territorial lands, old and new were confused, rent and tax were not timely, and merger should be added.
translations.idiomatic: Yong held many migrant communities. Xuanmo reported that refugee commanderies had no fixed territory, old and new registrations were tangled, and taxes came late. He proposed consolidation.

sentences.zh: 見許。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 乃省並郡縣，自此便之。

translations.literal: He then reduced and merged commanderies and counties; from this it was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He merged commanderies and counties, and administration grew simpler.

sentences.zh: 百姓當時不願屬籍。

translations.literal: The people at the time did not wish to be registered.
translations.idiomatic: The people did not want to be registered.

sentences.zh: 其年，玄謨又令九品以上租，使貧富相通，境內莫不嗟怨。

translations.literal: That year Xuanmo again ordered rent from those of ninth rank and above, making rich and poor share alike; within the borders none did not sigh and resent.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he levied rent from every household of ninth rank and above, forcing rich and poor to pay alike. Resentment spread through the province.

sentences.zh: 人間訛言玄謨欲反，時柳元景當權，元景弟僧景為新城太守，以元景之勢，制令雍土南陽順陽上庸新城諸郡併發兵，欲討玄謨。

translations.literal: Among the people false rumor spread that Xuanmo would rebel; at the time Liu Yuanjing held power; Yuanjing's younger brother Sengjing was Administrator of Xincheng; relying on Yuanjing's power he ordered the commanderies of Nanyang, Shunyang, Shangyong, and Xincheng in Yong all to raise troops, intending to attack Xuanmo.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Xuanmo meant to rebel. Liu Yuanjing held power then; his brother Sengjing governed Xincheng and, trading on that influence, ordered Nanyang, Shunyang, Shangyong, and Xincheng to mobilize against Xuanmo.

sentences.zh: 玄謨令內外晏然，以解眾惑，馳啟孝武，具陳本末。

translations.literal: Xuanmo ordered inside and outside to be calm to dispel the crowd's confusion; he galloped to report to Xiaowu and fully stated cause and effect.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo kept his province calm to quell panic, then galloped to Xiaowu with a full account.

sentences.zh: 帝知其虛，馳遣主書吳喜公慰撫之。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew it was false and galloped to send Chief Secretary Wu Xigong to comfort and soothe him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the charge was false, the emperor sent Chief Secretary Wu Xigong to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 又答曰：「玄謨啟明白之日，七十老公反欲何求？

translations.literal: He also replied, "On the day Xuanmo's memorial was clear—what would a seventy-year-old man seek by rebelling?
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote back, "The day your memorial arrived—a seventy-year-old man, what rebellion could he want?

sentences.zh: 聊復為笑，想足以申卿眉頭耳。

translations.literal: This is merely for laughter; I think it should be enough to smooth your brow."
translations.idiomatic: Take it as a joke—I trust that will unknit your brow."

sentences.zh: 」玄謨性嚴，未曾妄笑，時人言玄謨眉頭未曾申，故以此見戲。

translations.literal: Xuanmo's nature was stern; he never laughed without cause; men of the time said Xuanmo's brow had never smoothed, so they mocked him thus.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo was so stern he almost never laughed. People said his brow had never unknotted—hence the emperor's jest.

sentences.zh: 後為金紫光祿大夫，領太常。

translations.literal: Later he was Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 及建明堂，以本官領起部尚書，又領北選。

translations.literal: When the Bright Hall was built he held his original post and also directed the Ministry of Construction and also directed northern selection.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bright Hall was raised he kept his post, headed the construction ministry, and oversaw northern appointments.

sentences.zh: 孝武狎侮群臣，各有稱目，多須者謂之羊，短長肥瘦皆有比擬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu treated the ministers with familiarity and insult, each with a nickname; the bearded he called sheep; short, tall, fat, and thin all had comparisons.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu mocked his ministers with nicknames—bearded men were "sheep," and every build had its label.

sentences.zh: 顏師伯缺齒，號之曰齴，劉秀之儉吝，常呼為老慳。

translations.literal: Yan Shibo lacked teeth and was called Yan; Liu Xiuzhi was miserly and was often called Old Miser.
translations.idiomatic: Toothless Yan Shibo became "Gum." Stingy Liu Xiuzhi was "Old Miser."

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎宗靈秀軀體肥壯，拜起艱難，每一集會，輒於坐賜靈秀器服飲食，前後相系，欲其占謝傾踣，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zong Lingxiu had a stout body; rising and bowing were difficult; at every gathering the Emperor would at his seat bestow Lingxiu vessels, clothes, and food one after another, wishing him to rise to thank and stumble for laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zong Lingxiu was corpulent and bowed with difficulty. At every feast Xiaowu piled gifts on him hoping he would rise, stumble, and amuse the court.

sentences.zh: 又刻木作靈秀父光祿勳叔獻像送其家聽事。

translations.literal: He also carved wood into the image of Lingxiu's father, the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness Shuxian, and sent it to his family's reception hall.
translations.idiomatic: He carved a wooden statue of Lingxiu's father Shuxian and sent it to the family hall.

sentences.zh: 柳元景、垣護之雖並北人，而玄謨獨受老傖之目。

translations.literal: Though Liu Yuanjing and Yuan Huzhi were both northerners, only Xuanmo received the nickname Old Rustic.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing and Huzhi were northerners too, yet only Xuanmo was nicknamed Old Rustic.

sentences.zh: 凡諸稱謂，四方書疏亦如之。

translations.literal: All such appellations in letters from the four directions were likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Official correspondence from every quarter used the same nicknames.

sentences.zh: 嘗為玄謨作四時詩曰：「菫茹供春膳，粟漿充夏餐，瓟醬調秋菜，白醝解冬寒。

translations.literal: Once he made four-seasons poetry for Xuanmo, saying, "Taro feeds spring meals, millet gruel fills summer fare, gourd sauce seasons autumn dishes, white pickled vegetables relieve winter cold."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote seasonal verse for Xuanmo: "Taro for spring, millet gruel for summer, gourd sauce for autumn, white pickles against winter cold."

sentences.zh: 」又寵一昆侖奴子名白主，常在左右，令以杖擊群臣。

translations.literal: He also favored a Kunlun slave boy named Baizhu, always at his side, ordering him to strike ministers with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: He favored a Kunlun slave called Baizhu who walked at his side and beat ministers with a staff on command.

sentences.zh: 自柳元景以下皆罹其毒。

translations.literal: From Liu Yuanjing downward all suffered his abuse.
translations.idiomatic: From Liu Yuanjing down, none escaped the rod.

sentences.zh: 玄謨尋遷徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Xuanmo soon was transferred to Governor of Xuzhou with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo was soon transferred to Governor of Xuzhou with full command.

sentences.zh: 時北土災饉，乃散私谷十萬斛牛千頭以賑之。

translations.literal: At the time the north had disaster and famine; he distributed private grain of one hundred thousand hu and a thousand oxen to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck the north. He opened his granaries—one hundred thousand hu of grain and a thousand oxen.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，與群公俱被顧命。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu died Xuanmo was among the group entrusted with the final testament.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu died Xuanmo was named among the regents.

sentences.zh: 時朝政多門，玄謨以嚴直不容，徙青、冀二州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: At the time court affairs had many factions; Xuanmo because of stern uprightness could not tolerate it and was transferred to Governor of Qing and Ji with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Court factions multiplied. Too upright to endure them, Xuanmo was moved to govern Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 少帝誅顏師伯、柳元景等，狂悖滋甚，以領軍征玄謨，子侄咸勸稱疾。

translations.literal: When Shaodi executed Yan Shibo, Liu Yuanjing, and others, his wildness grew worse; he sent the Palace Guard to summon Xuanmo; sons and nephews all urged him to feign illness.
translations.idiomatic: After Shaodi murdered Yan Shibo and Liu Yuanjing his madness worsened. He summoned Xuanmo with the Palace Guard. Kin urged him to plead illness.

sentences.zh: 玄謨曰：「避難苟免，既乖事君之節，且吾荷先朝厚恩，彌不得逡巡。

translations.literal: Xuanmo said, "To flee disaster and seek exemption already fails the duty of serving one's lord; moreover I bear the former dynasty's deep grace—I absolutely cannot hesitate."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo refused. "To hide from danger is already disloyalty—and I owe the late emperor too much to hang back."

sentences.zh: 」及至，屢表諫諍，又流涕請緩刑去殺，以安元元之意。

translations.literal: When he arrived he repeatedly memorialized in remonstrance and wept begging to slow punishments and remove executions, to settle the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: At court he remonstrated again and again, weeping for milder punishments and an end to slaughter—for the people's sake.

sentences.zh: 少帝大怒。

translations.literal: Shaodi was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Shaodi was furious.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，禮遇益崇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded, courtesy and honor grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, honor only increased.

sentences.zh: 時四方反叛，玄謨領水軍前鋒南討，以腳疾未差，聽乘輿出入。

translations.literal: At the time the four directions rebelled; Xuanmo led the navy as vanguard for the southern punitive campaign; because his leg ailment was not yet healed he was permitted to ride in carriage in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion erupted everywhere. Xuanmo led the naval vanguard south; his leg still lame, he was allowed a carriage at court.

sentences.zh: 尋除車騎將軍、江州刺史，副司徒建安王休仁於赭圻，賜以諸葛亮筩袖鎧。

translations.literal: Soon he was made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Jiangzhou, assisting Minister Over the Masses Prince of Jian'an Xiuren at Zheqi, and was given Zhuge Liang's tube-sleeve armor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Jiangzhou, second to Prince of Jian'an Xiuren at Zheqi, and given Zhuge Liang's tube-sleeve armor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以為左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領護軍將軍，遷南豫州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: Presently he was made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand General with equal ceremony to the Three Dukes, Director of the Palace Guard, transferred to Governor of South Yu with added overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand General with Three Dukes ceremony, Director of the Palace Guard, and Governor of South Yu with full command.

sentences.zh: 薨年八十二，諡曰莊公。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-two; posthumous name Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-two with the posthumous title Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 寬弟瞻字明遠，一字叔鸞。

translations.literal: Xuanmo's younger brother Zhan, styled Mingyuan, also styled Shuluan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo's younger brother Zhan, styled Mingyuan and also Shuluan.

sentences.zh: 負氣傲俗，好貶裁人物。

translations.literal: He bore himself with proud spirit, scorned custom, and loved to belittle others.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and scornful of convention, he loved to cut others down.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為王府參軍。

translations.literal: He served Song as staff officer to a prince's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He served Song on a prince's staff.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣劉彥節，直登榻曰：「君侯是公孫，僕是公子，引滿促膝，唯餘二人。

translations.literal: Once he visited Liu Yanjie, mounted the couch straightway and said, "You, lord, are a duke's son; I am a marquis's son—let us fill our cups knee to knee, just us two."
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Liu Yanjie he climbed straight onto the couch. "You are a duke's son, I a marquis's son—let us drink knee to knee, just the two of us."

sentences.zh: 」彥節外跡雖酬之，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: Yanjie outwardly responded but inwardly was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjie answered politely but seethed inside.

sentences.zh: 齊豫章王嶷少時，早與瞻友。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yuzhang of Qi was young he had early been Zhan's friend.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang of Qi had been Zhan's friend since youth.

sentences.zh: 瞻常候嶷高論，齊武帝時在大床寢，瞻謂嶷曰：「帳中人物亦復隨人寢興。

translations.literal: Zhan often waited on Niao's lofty discussions; at the time Emperor Wu of Qi was sleeping on the great bed; Zhan told Niao, "The man in the tent rises and sleeps as others do."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan often debated with Niao while Qi Wudi slept on the great bed. Zhan told Niao, "Even the man in the tent sleeps and wakes like anyone else."

sentences.zh: 」嶷言次忽問王景文兄楷賢愚何如殷道矜，瞻曰：「卿遂復言他人兄邪。

translations.literal: In the midst of talk Niao suddenly asked how Wang Jingwen's elder brother Kai compared in worth to Yin Daojin; Zhan said, "You speak of another man's brother again?"
translations.idiomatic: Mid-conversation Niao asked whether Wang Kai was wiser than Yin Daojin. Zhan snapped, "Must you talk about someone else's brother?"

sentences.zh: 」武帝笑稱嶷小名阿玉，「汝兄愚，那得忽來王參軍此句」。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and called Niao's childhood name A'yu, "Your brother is foolish—how could he suddenly come out with Staff Officer Wang's line?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and called Niao by his childhood name A'yu. "Your brother is a fool—how did Staff Officer Wang's line come from him?"

sentences.zh: 瞻曰：「直恐如卿來談。

translations.literal: Zhan said, "I only fear he talks as you do."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan replied, "I only fear he talks the way you do."

sentences.zh: 」武帝銜之，未嘗形色。

translations.literal: The Emperor harbored resentment yet never showed it in face or color.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nursed the grudge but never showed it.

sentences.zh: 後曆黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he served as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及齊建元初，瞻為永嘉太守，詣闕跪拜不如儀。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan in Qi he was Administrator of Yongjia; coming to court his bow and kneel were not according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qi's Jianyuan era he governed Yongjia. At court his bow was improper.

sentences.zh: 武帝知之，召入東宮，仍送付廷尉殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew it and summoned him to the Eastern Palace, then sent him to the Court of Justice for execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew, summoned him to the Eastern Palace, then handed him to the Court of Justice for execution.

sentences.zh: 命左右啟高帝曰：「父辱子死；

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to report to Emperor Gao, "When the father is shamed the son dies;
translations.idiomatic: He told attendants to report to Emperor Gao, "When the father is insulted the son must die;

sentences.zh: 王瞻傲朝廷，臣輒已收之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhan insulted the court—I have already seized him."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan insulted the throne—I have already taken him."

sentences.zh: 」高帝曰：「此何足計。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said, "This is not worth reckoning."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "That is hardly worth mention."

sentences.zh: 」及聞瞻已死，乃默無言。

translations.literal: When he heard Zhan was already dead he then fell silent and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Zhan was already dead he said nothing.

sentences.zh: 玄謨從弟玄象，位下邳太守。

translations.literal: Xuanmo's cousin Xuanxiang held the post of Administrator of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo's cousin Xuanxiang was Administrator of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 好發塚，地無完槨。

translations.literal: He loved opening tombs; no ground had intact coffins.
translations.idiomatic: He robbed graves wherever he went; no tomb escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 人間垣內有小塚，墳上殆平，每朝日初升，見一女子立塚上，近視則亡。

translations.literal: Among the people within a wall was a small tomb whose mound was nearly level; each sunrise a woman stood on the mound; viewed close she vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city walls stood a small mound nearly level with the ground. At every sunrise a woman appeared on it and vanished when approached.

sentences.zh: 或以告玄象，便命發之。

translations.literal: Someone told Xuanxiang and he at once ordered it opened.
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Xuanxiang and he ordered it dug up at once.

sentences.zh: 有一棺尚全，有金蠶、銅人以百數。

translations.literal: One coffin was still whole, with gold silkworms and bronze figures numbering in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: One coffin remained intact, holding hundreds of gold silkworms and bronze figures.

sentences.zh: 剖棺見一女子，年可二十，姿質若生，臥而言曰：「我東海王家女，應生，資財相奉，幸勿見害。

translations.literal: Opening the coffin they saw a woman, about twenty years old, her beauty as if alive; lying she spoke, "I am a daughter of the Wang house of Donghai, about to be born; treasure is offered to you—please do not harm me."
translations.idiomatic: Inside lay a woman of about twenty, beautiful as if alive. She spoke from the coffin: "I am a daughter of the Wang house of Donghai, not yet born. Take the treasure—do not harm me."

sentences.zh: 」女臂有玉釧，破塚者斬臂取之，於是女復死。

translations.literal: On the woman's arm was a jade bracelet; the tomb-breakers cut off the arm to take it, and then the woman died again.
translations.idiomatic: A jade bracelet circled her arm. The robbers severed the arm to take it, and she died again.

sentences.zh: 玄謨時為徐州刺史，以事上聞，玄象坐免郡。

translations.literal: Xuanmo at the time was Governor of Xuzhou; he reported the affair upward; Xuanxiang was removed from his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo, then Governor of Xuzhou, reported the crime. Xuanxiang was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 玄載弟玄邈字彥遠，仕宋位青州刺史。

translations.literal: Xuanmo's younger brother Xuanyao's younger brother Xuanmiao, styled Yanyuan, served Song as Governor of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo's kinsman Xuanmiao, styled Yanyuan, served Song as Governor of Qing.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝之鎮淮陰，為宋明帝所疑，乃北勸魏，遣書結玄邈。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi garrisoned Huaiyin he was suspected by Emperor Ming of Song and therefore urged Wei from the north and sent letters to win Xuanmiao.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Wudi garrisoned Huaiyin, Song's Emperor Ming suspected him. He turned north to Wei and wrote to win Xuanmiao over.

sentences.zh: 玄邈長史房叔安進曰：「夫布衣韋帶之士，銜一餐而不忘，義使之然也。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao's chief clerk Fang Shuan advanced and said, "A man in cloth belt and hemp sash, receiving one meal does not forget—righteousness makes it so.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerk Fang Shuan protested: "A man in coarse clothes who remembers a single meal does so from righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今將軍居方州之重，托君臣之義，無故舉忠孝而棄之，三齊之士寧蹈東海死耳，不敢隨將軍也。

translations.literal: Now the general holds the weight of a frontier province, entrusted with the duty of lord and minister; to raise loyalty and filial piety and cast them aside for no reason—the men of the Three Qi would rather throw themselves into the eastern sea and die than follow the general."
translations.idiomatic: You hold a frontier province in the emperor's trust. To abandon loyalty and filial piety without cause—the men of the Three Qi would drown themselves in the eastern sea before they followed you."

sentences.zh: 」玄邈意乃定。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao's mind was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao's resolve steadied.

sentences.zh: 仍使叔安使建鄴，發高帝謀。

translations.literal: He still sent Shuan as envoy to Jiankang to expose Emperor Gao's plot.
translations.idiomatic: He still sent Shuan to Jiankang to expose Qi Wudi's plot.

sentences.zh: 高帝于路執之，並求玄邈表。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao on the road seized him and also demanded Xuanmiao's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wudi seized him on the road and demanded Xuanmiao's letter.

sentences.zh: 叔安答曰：「寡君使表上天子，不上將軍。

translations.literal: Shuan answered, "My lord sent the memorial to the Son of Heaven, not to the general.
translations.idiomatic: Shuan answered, "My lord's letter was for the Son of Heaven, not for you.

sentences.zh: 且僕之所言，利國家而不利將軍，無所應問。

translations.literal: Moreover what I say benefits the state and not the general—there is nothing to answer."
translations.idiomatic: And what I said serves the state, not you—there is nothing to tell you."

sentences.zh: 」荀伯玉勸殺之，高帝曰：「物各為主，無所責也。

translations.literal: Xun Boyu urged killing him; Emperor Gao said, "Things each have their master—there is nothing to blame."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Boyu urged execution. Qi Wudi said, "Each man serves his own lord—no blame in that."

sentences.zh: 」玄邈罷州還，高帝塗中要之，玄邈嚴軍直過。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao ended his governorship and returned; Emperor Gao waylaid him on the road; Xuanmiao drew up his army and passed straight through.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao left office and returned home. Qi Wudi ambushed him on the road. Xuanmiao marched his guard straight through.

sentences.zh: 還都，啟宋明帝，稱高帝有異謀，高帝不恨也。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he reported to Emperor Ming of Song that Emperor Gao had a different plot; Emperor Gao did not resent it.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he reported Qi Wudi's treachery to Song Mingdi. Qi Wudi bore no grudge.

sentences.zh: 升明中，高帝引為驃騎司馬、泰山太守。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era Emperor Gao summoned him as Rapid Cavalry Staff Major and Administrator of Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengming era Qi Wudi made him Rapid Cavalry staff major and Administrator of Taishan.

sentences.zh: 玄邈甚懼，高帝待之如初。

translations.literal: Xuanmiao was greatly afraid; Emperor Gao treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao was terrified. Qi Wudi treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 再遷西戎校尉、梁南秦二州刺史，封河陽縣侯，兄弟同時為方伯。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Colonel of the Western Rong and Governor of Liang and South Qin, enfeoffed as Marquis of Heyang; brothers at the same time were frontier governors.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Colonel of the Western Rong and Governor of Liang and South Qin, enfeoffed Marquis of Heyang—brothers governing frontiers together.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，亡命李烏奴作亂梁部，玄邈使人偽降烏奴，告之曰：「王使君兵弱，攜愛妾二人已去矣。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan in Qi the outlaw Li Wunu rebelled in Liang; Xuanmiao sent a man to feign surrender to Wunu and told him, "Lord Wang's troops are weak; he has already taken his two beloved concubines and gone."
translations.idiomatic: At Qi's founding the outlaw Li Wunu rebelled in Liang. Xuanmiao sent a false defector who told Wunu, "Lord Wang's force is weak—he has already fled with his two favorite concubines."

sentences.zh: 」烏奴喜，輕兵襲州城，玄邈奇兵破之。

translations.literal: Wunu rejoiced, led light troops to raid the provincial city; Xuanmiao's surprise troops defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wunu rejoiced, led light troops against the capital, and was crushed by Xuanmiao's ambush.

sentences.zh: 高帝聞之曰：「玄邈果不負吾。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gao heard and said, "Xuanmiao truly has not failed me."
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wudi heard it and said, "Xuanmiao has not failed me after all."

sentences.zh: 論曰：自晉室播遷，來宅揚、越，關邊遙阻，汧、隴遐荒，區甸分其內外，山河判其表裏。

translations.literal: Commentary says: From the time the Jin house was driven abroad and came to dwell in Yang and Yue, the frontier was far blocked, Qian and Long remote and wild; inner and outer were divided by districts, mountains and rivers marked inner from outer.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: After the Jin court fled south to Yang and Yue, the frontier lay far away and Qian-Long vanished into the wilderness. District lines split inner from outer; mountains and rivers drew the border.

sentences.zh: 桓溫一代英人，志移晉鼎，自非兵屈霸上，戰衄枋頭，則光宅之運，中年允集。

translations.literal: Huan Wen was a hero of his age, his will set on moving the Jin tripod; had he not been defeated in arms at Bashang and routed at Fangtou, the fortune of dwelling in the imperial capital would have gathered at mid-age.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen was the age's hero, intent on moving the throne. Had he not lost at Bashang and been routed at Fangtou, he might have restored the capital in his prime.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝屈起布衣，非藉人譽，一旦驅率烏合，奄興霸緒，功雖有餘而德猶未洽。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song rose from common cloth without borrowing others' reputation; in one stroke he drove and led a rabble host and suddenly raised hegemonic enterprise; merit though had surplus yet virtue was still not harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu rose from the ranks without borrowed fame. He welded a mob into an army and seized a hegemony overnight—merit aplenty, but virtue not yet settled.

sentences.zh: 非樹奇功於難立，震大威于四海，則不能成配天之業，一異同之心。

translations.literal: Unless he piled strange merit in hard establishment and shook great awe through the four seas, he could not accomplish the enterprise matching Heaven and unify hearts of difference.
translations.idiomatic: Without spectacular victories in impossible places and awe across the four seas, he could not win a Mandate of Heaven or bind divided hearts.

sentences.zh: 故須外積武功，以收人望。

translations.literal: Therefore he had to accumulate external martial achievement to gather men's regard.
translations.idiomatic: So he needed victories abroad to gather the people's gaze.

sentences.zh: 及金墉請吏，元勳既立，心欲掛旆龍門，折沖冀、趙，跨功桓氏，取高昔人。

translations.literal: When Jinyong asked for officials and the founding merit was established, his heart wished to hang banners at Longmen, break the enemy at Ji and Zhao, surpass Huan's achievement, and take height over men of old.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinyong submitted and the founding heroes stood firm, he dreamed of banners at Longmen, triumph in Ji and Zhao, surpassing Huan Wen and outdoing the ancients.

sentences.zh: 方復觀兵崤、渭，陳師天嶮。

translations.literal: He was about to review troops at Xiao and Wei and deploy armies at heaven's passes.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to parade at Xiao and Wei and mass armies at the sky's narrow gates.

sentences.zh: 及靈威薄震，重關自辟，故知英算所包，先勝而後戰也。

translations.literal: When spiritual might thinned and shook and the heavy passes opened of themselves, one knew that the hero's calculation embraced victory before battle.
translations.idiomatic: When his prestige alone shook the frontier and the passes fell open, one saw that his plans won before the fight began.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡推鋒直指，前無強陣，為宋方叔，其壯矣乎。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen'e thrust forward directly, with no strong array before him; as Song's Fangshu he was mighty indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e drove straight ahead with no enemy line able to stop him—Song's Fangshu, and mighty indeed.

sentences.zh: 朱齡石、超石、毛修之、傅弘之等，以歸眾難固之情，逢英勇乘機之運，以至顛陷，為不幸矣。

translations.literal: Zhu Lingshi, Chaoshi, Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi, and others, with the feeling that returning masses are hard to hold firm, met the fortune of brave men seizing opportunity, yet came to ruin and fall—how unfortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingshi, Chaoshi, Mao Xiuzhi, Fu Hongzhi, and the rest held armies hard to keep loyal in retreat, rode a tide of bold opportunity—and still fell. Ill fortune indeed.

sentences.zh: 修之滑台之守，有疏勒之難，苟誠節在焉，所在為重，其取榮大國，豈徒然哉。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's defense of Huatai had the hardship of Shule; if sincere integrity is present, wherever one stands carries weight; to gain glory in a great state—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xiuzhi's siege of Huatai had Shule's agony. Where integrity holds, a man's weight follows—and glory in a great kingdom is never empty.

sentences.zh: 終假道自歸，首丘之義也。

translations.literal: In the end he borrowed a road to return of himself—the righteousness of turning the head toward the home mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he found his way home—the old loyalty of facing one's birth mound.

sentences.zh: 玄謨封狼之心，雖簡帝念；

translations.literal: Xuanmo's heart to seal Wolf Mountain, though the Emperor kept it in mind;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmo's dream of Wolf Mountain the emperor shared;

sentences.zh: 然天方相魏，人豈能支。

translations.literal: yet Heaven was then aiding Wei—how could men support it?
translations.idiomatic: yet Heaven favored Wei then—what could men do?

sentences.zh: 宋氏以三吳之弱卒，當八州之勁勇，欲以邀勝，不亦難乎。

translations.literal: Song with the weak troops of the Three Wu facing the fierce courage of eight provinces, wishing to wrest victory—was it not hard?
translations.idiomatic: Song's soft Three-Wu soldiers against eight provinces of northern fury, hoping to win—was that not folly?

sentences.zh: 蹙境亡師，固其宜也。

translations.literal: Shrinking territory and losing armies—naturally it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Territory lost, armies broken—that was only fitting.

sentences.zh: 觀夫慶之言，可謂達于時變。

translations.literal: Seeing Qing's words one may say he understood the changes of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qingzhi's words show a man who read the times.

sentences.zh: 瞻傲佷不悔，卒至亡軀，然齊武追恨魚服，匹夫懼矣。

translations.literal: Zhan's arrogance and harshness without repentance led at last to loss of life; yet Qi Wu regretted the fish-skin coat—a common man would fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's arrogant defiance cost him his life; yet when Qi Wudi mourned the fish-skin robe, even a common man might tremble.

sentences.zh: 玄邈行己之度，有士君子之風乎。

translations.literal: Did Xuanmiao's measure in conducting himself have the air of a gentleman?
translations.idiomatic: Xuanmiao's conduct—did it not have something of the gentleman's way?
